==== Iris ====
Iris is a {{Florrverse/Petal}} {{Florrverse/Drop}}ped from Scorpions and Jungle Centipedes. 

The Iris {{Florrverse/Petal}} consists of a small circle, smaller than the Basic and has the same size as the Light. However, instead of being white-colored, it wields a lavender purple color with a darker shade of it on its borders. {{Florrverse/Flower}}s hit by an Iris will turn lavender purple (same color as an Iris) and will frown, regardless if they are defending or not.

The Iris poisons any enemy that touches it. The enemy will take the amount of {{Florrverse/Damage}} shown by the {{Florrverse/Petal}}'s poison stat. Despite only flashing every second, the poisoned entity will actually receive {{Florrverse/Damage}} every tick. 

The poison effect does not stack, however, hitting a poisoned enemy again with Iris (or any other poisonous {{Florrverse/Petal}}) will reset the poison value to either the current one or the one of the {{Florrverse/Petal}} that hit it, whichever is higher. It will not add poison onto the pre-existing value.

==== Pincer ====
Pincer is a {{Florrverse/Petal}} {{Florrverse/Drop}}ped by Scorpions. The Pincer looks like a black semicircle, but curved like a sickle, and looks like a burnt boomerang.

Upon contact, poisons the enemy and slows them down. The slowdown effect does stack with other Pincers.

The enemy will take the amount of {{Florrverse/Damage}} shown by the {{Florrverse/Petal}}'s poison stat at a rate determined by the poison's DPS.

Poison does not stack. Applying more poison before prior poison has ended will reset the poison value to either the current one or the one of the {{Florrverse/Petal}} that hit it, whichever is higher. It will not add poison onto the pre-existing value.

Pincer's poison effect is unremarkable, having smaller poison {{Florrverse/Damage}} than the Iris, although it does have a faster respawn. Pincer's main use is as a slowdown {{Florrverse/Petal}}, hindering an enemy's advance. 

The pincer has the strongest slowdown in the game, leaving enemies wide open for attack. However, it can't affect multiple targets at once like the Web and unlike Glass.

=== Desert Centipede ===
The Desert Centipede is a {{Florrverse/Mob}} that lives in the desert. It is passive until attacked; which means it is neutral.

Its front head is a light yellow circle with 2 black circles on its side and a pair of antennae. Its other segments are the same, the only difference being that they have no antennae.

Speed: The Desert Centipede is the third fastest {{Florrverse/Mob}} in the game, after the Leech and Roach (respectively).

Behavior: It moves randomly in any direction, changing direction when it hits the edge of the map. When a Desert Centipede gets split into multiple parts, or a part gets its head destroyed, any new parts go in a random direction if it is{{Florrverse/Rare}} {{Florrverse/Rank}} or below. Every few seconds, the centipede can go "under the sand", which is when they turn greyed out and aren't able to attack or be attacked.

It {{Florrverse/Drop}}s Salt and Powder.

==== Salt ====
Salt is a {{Florrverse/Petal}} that is {{Florrverse/Drop}}ped by Desert Centipedes and Starfish. It is a white heptagon with a light-gray border, resembling the irregular shape of a Rock.

Reflects some incoming {{Florrverse/Damage}} back at the entity that dealt it. For each Rank below the listed Rank, it will reflect triple the {{Florrverse/Damage}} received: for example, {{Florrverse/Super}} Salt reflects 100{{Florrverse/%}} against {{Florrverse/Super}} {{Florrverse/Mob}}s, 300{{Florrverse/%}} against {{Florrverse/Ultra}} {{Florrverse/Mob}}s, and 900{{Florrverse/%}} against {{Florrverse/Mythic}} {{Florrverse/Mob}}s. It reflects 20{{Florrverse/%}} {{Florrverse/Damage}} against other {{Florrverse/Flower}}s. Doesn't stack with other salts.

The best defense is a good offense. Salt serves as a useful defensive {{Florrverse/Petal}} to {{Florrverse/Flower}}s, countering enemy attacks should they {{Florrverse/Damage}} the {{Florrverse/User}}. Not only does this work against collisions, this also defends against ranged attacks. However, using Salt effectively requires the {{Florrverse/Flower}} to get hit often, which is usually a risky strategy and works best with builds full of healing {{Florrverse/Petal}}s. Against higher-Rank {{Florrverse/Mob}}s, the {{Florrverse/Damage}} likely won't be enough to kill the {{Florrverse/Mob}} before a {{Florrverse/Flower}} is killed, and Salt returns to being a supporting {{Florrverse/Petal}}.

==== Powder ====
Powder is a {{Florrverse/Petal}} {{Florrverse/Drop}}ped from Desert Centipedes. Powder consists of a white splatter of paint. While being used, it animates and shifts around like it is being blown apart.

Powder gives {{Florrverse/Flower}}s more movement speed, and its speed bonus does not stack with other Powders. It destroys itself when {{Florrverse/Flower}}s approach a {{Florrverse/Mob}} with a Rank higher than the specified Rank or when {{Florrverse/Flower}}s take {{Florrverse/Damage}}.

Powder is intended for fast travel between different areas and can be used with Bubbles for a faster speed. However, it has one downside: it gets destroyed if {{Florrverse/Flower}}s walk over a {{Florrverse/Mob}} that's higher than the maximum Rank of Powder. It is recommended for {{Florrverse/Flower}}s to use Cotton if they are using this with a Bubble build since low Rank {{Florrverse/Mob}}s can destroy their Powder if they are not careful.

=== Shiny Ladybug ===
Desert Ladybug is a {{Florrverse/Mob}} in the {{Florrverse/Florrverse}} that spawns in the Desert. It looks like a normal ladybug, except that it is yellow and has a dark yellow outline.

Its speed and behavior are the same as those of a normal ladybug. The Shiny Ladybug can spawn in Desert. There is no known Shiny Ladybug zone currently. It spawns most frequently at the {{Florrverse/Flower}} spawn area (1{{Florrverse/%}}), however it mainly spawns at low rarities.

The Shiny Ladybug {{Florrverse/Drop}}s Rose, Dahlia, and the famous Yggdrasil.

==== Dahlia ====
Dahlia is a {{Florrverse/Petal}} that {{Florrverse/Flower}}s can equip. Dahlia looks like 3 smaller Rose {{Florrverse/Petal}}s grouped together into a triangular shape, but it doesn't reduce the amount of space between {{Florrverse/Petal}}s, unlike other multiple- {{Florrverse/Petal}}s-in-one-slot like Light, meaning that the mini Roses stay close to each other.

Dahlia heals its {{Florrverse/User}} and allied {{Florrverse/Flower}}s with its mini-Roses. After the cooldown timer, the {{Florrverse/Petal}} is "consumed" by the {{Florrverse/Flower}}, who gains a certain amount of HP. It can't be given to friendly {{Florrverse/Mob}}s, like the Digger. Dahlia can be affected by the Duplicator Talent which gives one more mini Rose for the {{Florrverse/Petal}}.

Dahlia is more defensive than the rose, and also if one mini rose dies, the others are unharmed until they run out of {{Florrverse/Health}}.

==== Yggdrasil ====
This {{Florrverse/Petal}} is special; it can revive any {{Florrverse/Flower}}, but prevents them from being revived again for a certain time, after which they can. Yggdrasil looks like a short, brown leaf with a darker brown outline and lines through the middle.

Yggdrasil can revive a dead {{Florrverse/Flower}}, hence it's extreme popularity. It works like a Rose, but instead it revives any defeated {{Florrverse/Flower}}s and also heals the revived {{Florrverse/Flower}}s by all of their {{Florrverse/Health}}. When it is laid on a {{Florrverse/Flower}}, they come back to life after a certain duration and are invincible for 5 seconds. After being revived, the {{Florrverse/Flower}} is unrevivable for a certain amount of time, depending on the Yggdrasil's {{Florrverse/Rank}}.

Yggdrasil has the extremely powerful and useful ability of being able to revive a dead {{Florrverse/Flower}}. If a {{Florrverse/Flower}} dies, they will be left as a corpse, and they must travel back from the last checkpoint, which can take a long time and may be hard to do in some cases. For this reason, Yggdrasil is considered a necessity in squads; groups of {{Florrverse/Flower}}s that act like a team.

=== Cactus ===
Cacti are stationary {{Florrverse/Mob}}s that reside in the Desert of the {{Florrverse/Florrverse}}. It is a green circle with a dark green outline. It has thorns (which appear as black triangles) sticking out of the sides that work like dandelions but do not fire. The circle slightly bulges where the thorns are.

It doesn't do anything. Cacti do not pose much of a threat besides blockage. They have lots of body {{Florrverse/Damage}}, so it is recommended for {{Florrverse/Flower}}s to defeat them before they get launched into it by scorpions or other {{Florrverse/Mob}}s.

In Desert, the main danger to {{Florrverse/Flower}}s when fighting a {{Florrverse/Super}} {{Florrverse/Mob}} is not the actual {{Florrverse/Mob}}, but the many {{Florrverse/Ultra}}-{{Florrverse/Rank}}ed {{Florrverse/Mob}}s that spawn around the cactus. {{Florrverse/Flower}}s usually clear {{Florrverse/Mob}}s around it to make sure they don't get launched into it.

{{Florrverse/Flower}}s also don't ram into it, and it {{Florrverse/Drop}}s the {{Florrverse/Petal}} Cactus.

==== Cactus ( {{Florrverse/Petal}}) ====
Cactus is a {{Florrverse/Petal}} {{Florrverse/Drop}}ped by the Cactus. It's not very strong, but it increases {{Florrverse/Flower}}s' {{Florrverse/Health}}. Cactus consists of an eight-sided green {{Florrverse/Petal}}. Cactus's sides, while they are sharp in one end, are curvy on their beginning. Due to that, Cactus appears pointy, mimicking a real-life cactus's appearance. The {{Florrverse/Petal}} also has a light green circle in the center, indicating a font of light shining on it, while also being surrounded by an even darker green outline.

When it is equipped, Cactus increases the {{Florrverse/User}}'s maximum {{Florrverse/Health}} by some certain amount, which is dependent on the {{Florrverse/Petal}}'s {{Florrverse/Rank}}. Cactus is stackable. Cactus is {{Florrverse/Common}}ly used for ramming builds by {{Florrverse/Flower}}s, due to the {{Florrverse/Health}} increase. Thus, Cactus is found in {{Florrverse/Flower}}s with many other healing, cacti, and {{Florrverse/Health}} or body {{Florrverse/Damage}} related {{Florrverse/Petal}}s.

=== Sandstorm ===
Sandstorm is a passive but deadly {{Florrverse/Mob}} that lives in the Desert. It has the appearance of 3 hexagons, the biggest one is on the outside and is bright yellow. It spins clockwise. The second one is more dark and spins counter clockwise. The third, which is in the middle, spins clockwise like the first one and is the darkest.

It is faster than {{Florrverse/Flower}}s, but in unpredictable directions. {{Florrverse/Flower}}s are aware of its high body {{Florrverse/Damage}} and they usually use Third Eye to take it out from a distance if possible. {{Florrverse/Flower}}s are careful with these {{Florrverse/Mob}}s.

As higher-Rank Sandstorms are huge and can phase through {{Florrverse/Mob}}s, they can conceal {{Florrverse/Mob}}s from view, which could ambush {{Florrverse/Flower}}s if they get too close to the Sandstorm. Sandstorm {{Florrverse/Drop}}s Sand, Glass, and Stick.

==== Sand ====
Sand is a {{Florrverse/Petal}}. The Sand {{Florrverse/Petal}} consists of 4 small hexagons. Each hexagon is yellow with a dark yellow outline. The hexagons are arranged in a square shape. Unlike Light, all of the {{Florrverse/Petal}}s occupy the same spot. This applies to some {{Florrverse/Petal}}s like the Stinger.

Sand is a {{Florrverse/Damage}}/second-based {{Florrverse/Petal}} similar to the Light, having low {{Florrverse/Damage}} and {{Florrverse/Health}} but fast respawn. Compared to the Light, the Sand deals more burst {{Florrverse/Damage}} but less consistently. Sand also doesn't decrease the distance between other {{Florrverse/Petal}}s.

Sand is used by {{Florrverse/Flower}}s dealing with Hornets, Beetles, and other {{Florrverse/Mob}}s.

{{Florrverse/Flower}}s also use Sand as a shield sometimes.

==== Stick ====
Stick is a {{Florrverse/Petal}} that summons with the force of the wind. It resembles a cartoonish wooden stick.

The Stick is a bit worthy in different conditional ways for {{Florrverse/Flower}}s to use this {{Florrverse/Petal}}.

Compared to the other two summoning {{Florrverse/Petal}}s, Beetle Eggs and Ant Eggs, the Sticks summon much more powerful {{Florrverse/Mob}}s. 2 Sandstorms deal much more total {{Florrverse/Damage}} than both Eggs, while their total {{Florrverse/Health}} is higher than Beetle Eggs but lower than Ant Eggs. Because of this, civilisations thought it was unbalanced and decided to nerf it.

Just one stick, once both Sandstorms are spawned, has over 3x the burst {{Florrverse/Damage}} compared to a Beetle Egg. This makes it very powerful for resting {{Florrverse/Flower}}s as it can build up Sandstorms for a lurer. When using Sticks, it is recommended that {{Florrverse/Flower}}s use them against a wall to minimize the effect of the Sandstorm’s random movement. Stick excels in farming areas such as Sewers and Fire Ant Hell.

=== Fire Ants (of the Desert) ===
Fire Ants are variants of Ants that can spawn in Desert and Ant Hell. There are several versions. We are only talking about two, because the rest cannot spawn in Desert, so they will be mentioned in an unfinished section.

==== Fire Ant Burrows ====
Fire Ant Burrows are {{Florrverse/Mob}}s that spawn in the Desert. 3 Circles with a brighter red on the outside, darker red in the second circle, and the darkest in the middle circle. It is smaller than a regular Ant Hole.

{{Florrverse/Flower}}s usually don't come close to them when they are near other {{Florrverse/Mob}}s. They summon Soldier Fire Ants and {{Florrverse/Drop}} Discs and Magnets.

===== Disc =====
The Disc looks like a large, thick and black ring. Disc reduces all incoming collision {{Florrverse/Damage}} received between {{Florrverse/Mob}}s and {{Florrverse/Flower}}s by a certain percentage. The effect does not stack with each other. Highest Rank and the 1st slot in the build will be prioritised.

{{Florrverse/Flower}}s use several strategies with this {{Florrverse/Petal}}.

* The Disc's most reliable place to be used is in ram builds: it allows {{Florrverse/Flower}}s to take less {{Florrverse/Damage}}, letting them land more hits on {{Florrverse/Mob}}s before having to retreat and heal. Pairing this with Basil and passive heals can possibly outheal most enemies, with Cutter will give them more body {{Florrverse/Damage}} per hit while them take less {{Florrverse/Damage}}, while this and Cactus will give you more HP to let them deal more hits, and finally, this and Cutter will further decrease the amount of hits them need to land in order to kill a {{Florrverse/Mob}}.
* Disc can also work well with Relic, Root and Shell. Relic will further spread {{Florrverse/Damage}} taken if other {{Florrverse/Mob}}s are nearby, or use Ant Eggs with this and Relic instead to share {{Florrverse/Damage}} taken with the spawned Soldier Termites. Root will give them armor while you're in the defensive state, allowing {{Florrverse/Flower}}s to take an even smaller amount of {{Florrverse/Damage}} per ram. Shell will give them a shield meter for them to hit even more times.
* Another great {{Florrverse/Petal}} for using alongside Disc is Salt, as {{Florrverse/Flower}}s will take {{Florrverse/Damage}} from the enemy entity while dealing {{Florrverse/Damage}} to them, thus Salt will reflect some percentage of the {{Florrverse/Damage}} taken to them back to the enemy, further damaging them.

===== Magnet =====
Magnet allows the {{Florrverse/User}} to pick up {{Florrverse/Drop}}ped {{Florrverse/Petal}}s from farther away. This effect is only active when the {{Florrverse/Petal}} is alive, meaning pickup range will be reverted to normal when it is destroyed or is into recharge. Magnet does not expand upon attacking, and does not stack with itself; however, it stacks with the Magnetism talent. For example, a {{Florrverse/Flower}} using {{Florrverse/Ultra}} Magnet with Magnetism talent increases its pickup range by 1,000 {{Florrverse/+}} 960 = 1,960.

Magnet appears like a real magnet, with the left half being red and the right half being blue.

==== Soldier Fire Ant ====
The Soldier Fire Ant is a deadly {{Florrverse/Mob}} in the {{Florrverse/Florrverse}}. It deals twice the {{Florrverse/Damage}} of a Soldier Ant and also can see farther. It looks like a Soldier Ant except with a reddish-brown color. It is slow when it doesn't see a target, but it becomes as fast as a {{Florrverse/Flower}} when chasing one.

They come in large swarms in the Desert and Ant Hell since they spawn when a Fire Ant Burrow is attacked, all at once. Soldier Fire Ants {{Florrverse/Drop}} Yucca and Triangle.

===== Yucca =====
Yucca is a {{Florrverse/Petal}} that {{Florrverse/Flower}}s can equip. It is similar to the Leaf {{Florrverse/Petal}} except that it only heals {{Florrverse/Flower}}s in the devensive position, heals quicker, and it has less {{Florrverse/Damage}} than the leaf. It starts at the {{Florrverse/Unusual}} {{Florrverse/Rank}}.

Yucca looks like a thin, yellowish green leaf. It has a dark green outline and a dark green stripe through the middle. Unlike the Leaf {{Florrverse/Petal}}, it has two pointed ends, and no stem. {{Florrverse/Common}} Yuccas cannot be {{Florrverse/Drop}}ped and {{Florrverse/Super}} Yuccas have to be crafted.

The Yucca {{Florrverse/Petal}} itself is rather weak. The Yucca only heals the {{Florrverse/User}} when they are in defensive position, so Yuccas are best used alongside {{Florrverse/Petal}}s that work fine when in the defensive position.

===== Triangle =====
Triangle is a special {{Florrverse/Petal}}. It adds {{Florrverse/Damage}} to other triangles of the same {{Florrverse/Rank}}. Its color is white with a light gray outline.

Triangle affects other Triangles of the same Rank (except Triangles of the {{Florrverse/Unique}} & {{Florrverse/Eternal}} {{Florrverse/Rank}}, which is only buffed by {{Florrverse/Super}} Triangles) depending on how many other Triangles there are. For example, with three{{Florrverse/Legendary}} Triangles, each of them would do 405 {{Florrverse/+}} 324 × 2 = 1,053 {{Florrverse/Damage}}.

Triangles are very powerful, at around the same power as the {{Florrverse/Petal}} Glass.

== Species - Of The Ocean ==
The ocean is a diverse place with a lot of species.

=== Bubble ===
Bubble is a {{Florrverse/Mob}} that appears as a non-hued translucent circle with a white shine. It moves very slowly, moves around in various directions, and sometimes spins around. Bubble is immune to poison and chained lightning {{Florrverse/Damage}}.

This {{Florrverse/Mob}} has very low {{Florrverse/Health}}. However, it has high armor, a stat where {{Florrverse/Damage}}s less than the armor don't count, while {{Florrverse/Damage}}s more than the armor do count. Despite the armor, Bubbles are very easy to kill.

The {{Florrverse/Super}} Bubble is one of the hardest of this {{Florrverse/Rank}} to loot, as it will mostly die almost immediately after spawning due to very fast Bubble {{Florrverse/User}}s killing the Bubble before anyone else can reach it, or by {{Florrverse/Flower}}s already in ocean that are farming, killing it almost instantly.

Bubble {{Florrverse/Drop}}s the {{Florrverse/Petal}} Air and Bubble.

==== Air ====
Air is a {{Florrverse/Petal}} from the {{Florrverse/Florrverse}}. Its function consists of increasing the size of {{Florrverse/User}}s. Air consists of thin air, or, as its description makes clear, Air appears to be literally nothing. The description that {{Florrverse/Flower}}s made up is "It's literally nothing".

At first, Air appears to be literally nothing. However, once equipped, it increases the {{Florrverse/Flower}}'s size (and consequently its hitbox) by a certain amount. Technically, it also increases {{Florrverse/Petal}} attack radius (due to the increased body pushing out the {{Florrverse/Petal}}s), as well as the distance of {{Florrverse/Petal}}s between each other (as it won't appear in your {{Florrverse/Petal}} orbit). It doesn't stack, meaning that more Airs won't further increase the size of the {{Florrverse/User}}. However, Soil's own {{Florrverse/Flower}} size buff is able to stack with Air's buff.

Air has an extremely high {{Florrverse/Drop}} rate, so farming it is easy. Air is also frequently traded for coins.

Air is also very important in fighting and defeating {{Florrverse/Super}} Sandstorms since it sucks in {{Florrverse/Flower}}s, and {{Florrverse/Super}} Air makes the sucking effect less, but it also makes {{Florrverse/Flower}}s more vulnerable to Scorpion Missiles.

Before the modification that civilisations did that removed the Absorbing mechanic, Air used to do nothing, thus simply "removing" a {{Florrverse/Petal}} slot. Now, it increases the {{Florrverse/User}}'s radius, like Soil. However, unlike Air, Soil stacks, increases radius by 10 per {{Florrverse/Petal}} on all rarities, increases the {{Florrverse/User}}'s HP and decreases the {{Florrverse/User}}'s speed, while Air increases by a set amount each Rank, is unstackable and doesn't affect the {{Florrverse/User}}'s HP and speed. Soil is still able to stack with Air.

Air mostly brings no major benefit besides the Sandstorm one, and it mostly detriments {{Florrverse/Flower}}s.

==== Bubble ====
Bubble is a vital {{Florrverse/Petal}} {{Florrverse/Drop}}ped by the {{Florrverse/Mob}} Bubble. Bubble consists of a very bright shade of a transparent white. An even brighter ring surrounds the outside of the {{Florrverse/Petal}}, as well as a lighter dot in the upper right of the {{Florrverse/Petal}}, both having the same color and opacity.

{{Florrverse/Flower}}s can control when Bubble propels them in the opposite direction of where it was (prior to popping) relative to them. This effect stacks with other Bubbles, but if they are in certain directions, they can cancel out entirely. In other words, Bubbles close together will propel the {{Florrverse/User}} even further, while Bubbles exactly on the opposite sides of each other will fully or partially cancel out themselves.

It also pushes the movement of other {{Florrverse/Petal}}s forward, albeit a bit delayed when compared to the {{Florrverse/Flower}} itself. When Moon Rock is influencing the {{Florrverse/Flower}}'s {{Florrverse/Petal}} orbit, it is susceptible to all Bubbles revolving around it, being treated as the {{Florrverse/Flower}} itself and being propelled with the same velocity and direction as a {{Florrverse/Flower}} would.

One effective method that {{Florrverse/Flower}}s use to obtain {{Florrverse/Ultra}} bubbles once they already have a few {{Florrverse/Ultra}}s is placing ankh in a zone where {{Florrverse/Mob}}s do not spawn in crab kingdom, and then clear {{Florrverse/Mob}}s to reach {{Florrverse/Ultra}} bubbles({{Florrverse/Mob}}s). Then, if there are other {{Florrverse/Ultra}} {{Florrverse/Mob}}s blocking the path, they can lure them out, then swap their ankh to teleport to safety.

Bubble is solely a Utility {{Florrverse/Petal}}, as it is great for travelling. This makes bubble one of the most {{Florrverse/Common}} {{Florrverse/Petal}}s in the game.

=== Crab ===
Crab is one of the {{Florrverse/Mob}}s that spawns in the Ocean and at the top of Jungle near the Ocean portal. It is a hostile {{Florrverse/Mob}} that has a {{Florrverse/Unique}} attack pattern. Crabs have a slight red-brown oval, as a shell, consisting of 8 brown legs that move around while their moving. Some legs appear to have 2 lines. They also have 2 brown claws, which look identical to the {{Florrverse/Petal}} form. On its shells, 2 darker curved lines can also be found.

Its attack consists of moving towards the {{Florrverse/Flower}} that is its target, and instead of rushing towards them, they will orbit around the target. If the {{Florrverse/Flower}} is moving or after a certain period of time, the Crab will dash into that direction for a few seconds, sometimes hitting the target. After that, it will begin to orbit around the {{Florrverse/Flower}} again and repeat the cycle until they or the {{Florrverse/Flower}} are defeated. While dashing, they move faster.

Due to this, {{Florrverse/Flower}}s have reported crab being an annoying {{Florrverse/Mob}}. Crab has a {{Florrverse/Unique}} attack pattern compared to others. The Crab spawns mostly in Ocean. It is best for {{Florrverse/Flower}}s to stay aware when to fight or flee and of the Crabs attacking. They usually fight crabs in an open area.

Crabs are quite faster than {{Florrverse/Flower}}s, so they may likely get hit especially if the crab has a lot of {{Florrverse/Health}} and {{Florrverse/Damage}}.

Crabs {{Florrverse/Drop}} Sand & Claw.

==== Claw ====
The {{Florrverse/Petal}} looks almost exactly like a claw the Crab itself has: a claw-shaped {{Florrverse/Petal}} with a dark maroon color and an even darker outline. Claw differs from the other {{Florrverse/Petal}}s in that it will deal 20x its normal {{Florrverse/Damage}} when the victim has 80{{Florrverse/%}} or more of its {{Florrverse/Health}} left. Bonus hits will deal 20x the {{Florrverse/Damage}} of a normal hit. Bonus hits will be half as effective against enemy {{Florrverse/Flower}}s.

Unlike most {{Florrverse/Petal}}s, the Claw is more offensive or has more offensive value than defensive initially. Higher {{Florrverse/Rank}}s of Claws can clear higher {{Florrverse/Rank}}s of {{Florrverse/Mob}}s more easily. When {{Florrverse/Flower}}s use this {{Florrverse/Petal}}, they usually switch it once the {{Florrverse/Damage}} bonus ends.

=== Jellyfish ===
Jellyfish is a {{Florrverse/Mob}} that resides in the Ocean of the {{Florrverse/Florrverse}}. Jellyfish is a translucent white circle with 8 white lines near the circle's rim. It attacks by using lightning strikes; a special type of attack where the victim transfers its {{Florrverse/Damage}} in a chain of a certain length, based on the {{Florrverse/Petal}}'s {{Florrverse/Rank}}.

The {{Florrverse/Petal}} against Jellyfish is the {{Florrverse/Petal}} Rubber. Rubber is the best {{Florrverse/Petal}} to counter Jellyfish's lightning. Rubbers of the same Rank or higher will nullify it completely. {{Florrverse/Flower}}s often use Sponge in Ocean, taking it off once they are taking too much {{Florrverse/Damage}} from it and then not dying because of Second Chance. However, Jellyfish often kill them before they can heal or re-equip the Sponge. This makes Jellyfish very obnoxious.

Jellyfish {{Florrverse/Drop}}s the {{Florrverse/Petal}}s Lightning & Jelly.

==== Lightning ====
Lightning is a {{Florrverse/Petal}} from the {{Florrverse/Florrverse}}. Whenever it strikes an entity, the {{Florrverse/Petal}} releases a lightning discharge that {{Florrverse/Damage}}s several nearby enemies in a chain, while also briefly stunning them completely. Lightning is {{Florrverse/Drop}}ped by Jellyfish. The number of enemies in a chain varies by {{Florrverse/Rank}}, and lightning uses the same attack as Jellyfish does.

The Lightning looks like a small light blue star, with 10 pointy edges evenly distributed around itself.

The Lightning activates upon contact with enemy {{Florrverse/Mob}}s, {{Florrverse/Flower}}s or Assemblers. Once activated, the Lightning discharges a lightning bolt which can bounce to nearby enemies up to the indicated number of times by the bounce stat, based on the {{Florrverse/Rank}}, damaging every enemy struck by the lightning in the process. Lightnings actually do not activate on contact with projectiles such as missiles.

Although lightning has a {{Florrverse/Health}} stat, it instantly destroys itself upon contact with {{Florrverse/Mob}}s, preventing multihitting. Bubbles are also completely immune to lightning.

Lightning is a pretty decent overall {{Florrverse/Petal}} that could be used in a lot of moments. Usually, they would be used in swarms due to their special attack, because when that happens, it defeats many of the {{Florrverse/Mob}}s in the swarm.

Lightning has a slightly larger hitbox than most {{Florrverse/Petal}}s, allowing it to be a good defense against projectiles. 

Despite being affected by {{Florrverse/Petal}} {{Florrverse/Health}} talents, it doesn't matter for Lightning. It just makes Lightning much more durable against projectiles.

==== Jelly ====
Jelly is a {{Florrverse/Petal}} from the {{Florrverse/Florrverse}}. The Jelly's appearance is similar to the Bubble. However, instead of being transparent-white, it's purple-colored and looks more translucent. It also has five smaller purple circles on its body instead of only one.

The Jelly is average in stats, which are identical to a Basic. However, the Jelly has a knockback stat in which it will push {{Florrverse/Mob}}s away by a certain distance, (indicated by the knockback value) which varies by {{Florrverse/Rank}}, once they are touched by this {{Florrverse/Petal}}. The knockback stat differs from multi-hitting knockbacks.

Jelly is generally used when {{Florrverse/Flower}}s are cornered or {{Florrverse/Mob}}s are too close.

=== Leech ===
Leeches are alarmingly fast {{Florrverse/Mob}}s in the {{Florrverse/Florrverse}}. They appear similarly to Baby Ants, except that their body is lengthened. Leeches move much faster than {{Florrverse/Flower}}s when they are provoked. They slowly move around if they see it, then attack when they are close enough. When they latch on the targeted {{Florrverse/Flower}}, they attach onto it and deal {{Florrverse/Damage}} while also gaining {{Florrverse/Health}}.

Leeches are not actually made of a solid body, but instead they are made of several segments that share {{Florrverse/Health}}, and Lightning can deal a lot of {{Florrverse/Damage}} to it, with some {{Florrverse/Rank}}s dealing 630K {{Florrverse/Damage}} to the Leech.

{{Florrverse/Flower}}s {{Florrverse/Common}}ly counter Leeches by using a ramming build, and healing {{Florrverse/Petal}}s are required as it will still deal {{Florrverse/Damage}} to the {{Florrverse/Flower}}. Using egg {{Florrverse/Petal}}s like Ant Egg and Beetle Egg can be good when a lot of leeches are chasing you as it can make some of the leeches targeting them for a moment. Also, it can attack the leech from a far distance.

Leeches ram into {{Florrverse/Flower}}s and "suck their blood", draining {{Florrverse/Flower}} {{Florrverse/Health}}. Even though leeches can only "suck blood" once per second, ramming into the side of leeches of the{{Florrverse/Legendary}} {{Florrverse/Rank}} or higher can deal extreme {{Florrverse/Damage}}.

Even though Leeches of {{Florrverse/Rank}}s between and including {{Florrverse/Common}} and {{Florrverse/Mythic}} are not very tough, Leeches of the {{Florrverse/Ultra}} {{Florrverse/Rank}} can are able to defeat {{Florrverse/Flower}}s alone that is using a regular Ocean build; In return, {{Florrverse/Flower}}s usually tend to use mass-healing {{Florrverse/Petal}}s that are capable of being used in the defense position, alongside a few Fangs to heal back some of the massive amounts of {{Florrverse/Health}} that would be lost in the fight. Using a Disc also helps the {{Florrverse/User}}, a {{Florrverse/Flower}}, taking less {{Florrverse/Damage}} and therefore less healing required for recovery, making defeating the Leech easier and less risky.

Leech {{Florrverse/Drop}}s Fang and Faster, since its appearance has Fangs and it is incredibly fast.

==== Fang ====
Fang looks like a crimson diamond with rounded edges on the two corners in the middle and a dark red border. Fang is different from other healing {{Florrverse/Petal}}s: it heals the {{Florrverse/User}} only when it deals {{Florrverse/Damage}}. {{Florrverse/Damage}} dealt to any projectiles does not count. Fangs with an {{Florrverse/Unusual}} to {{Florrverse/Mythic}} {{Florrverse/Rank}} heal 35{{Florrverse/%}} of the {{Florrverse/Damage}} done by the {{Florrverse/Petal}}, while Fangs with a {{Florrverse/Rank}} of {{Florrverse/Ultra}} or higher heal less to match the scaling of healing {{Florrverse/Petal}}s. The percentage of {{Florrverse/Damage}} healed is affected by the Medic talent.

Areas lacking {{Florrverse/Mob}}s that launch projectiles like Scorpion and Hornet are preferable because {{Florrverse/Damage}} dealt to projectiles doesn't count. Despite the similar absence of projectile {{Florrverse/Mob}}s, Sewers is home to Flies which possess 90{{Florrverse/%}} {{Florrverse/Damage}} evasion and comprise 40{{Florrverse/%}} of the {{Florrverse/Mob}}s there.

Fang should be used carefully; if it is with the wrong {{Florrverse/Petal}}s (or rather most of the time), Fang may be rendered useless and should be traded for a coin. Fang also becomes useful only with a specific build. Fang is {{Florrverse/Common}}ly replaced by other {{Florrverse/Petal}}s when there are no {{Florrverse/Mob}}s that are in close proximity to the {{Florrverse/User}}.

Fang has a base {{Florrverse/Health}} of 1 and is the same for all {{Florrverse/Rank}}s, although the {{Florrverse/Damage}} differs and its base is 45 at the {{Florrverse/Unusual}} {{Florrverse/Rank}}. It has a {{Florrverse/Reload}} of 3.5 seconds and it starts at the {{Florrverse/Unusual}} {{Florrverse/Rank}}.

For biomes involving projectile spam or high-armor {{Florrverse/Mob}}s, one should consider using consistent and reliable healing options, such as Dahlia which {{Florrverse/Drop}}s from some Ladybugs, Leaf that is very highly accessable and Starfish, preferably with Sponge. Because of this, Fang is most frequently used in {{Florrverse/Garden}}.

=== Shell ===
The Shell is a {{Florrverse/Mob}} from the {{Florrverse/Florrverse}} derived from florr.io. Normally, it is im{{Florrverse/Mob}}ile, but it darts towards {{Florrverse/Flower}}s once every couple seconds after they {{Florrverse/Damage}} it. Shell has a hand fan shape with beige color and a darker outline, with two pairs of two lines, Each pair are shaped as a "V" shape and are placed in left-to-right position.

It is neutral. When provoked, lays down "giant" pearls (it shoots the pearls if it is in the {{Florrverse/Super}} {{Florrverse/Rank}}). It will then shake a couple times and suck the pearls back to itself. It also darts at its target every couple seconds, blasting you backwards or potentially crushing them into a wall.

Shells also have a shield that must be destroyed first before {{Florrverse/Flower}}s are able to bring down the actual {{Florrverse/Health}} of the Shell, making it act like extra {{Florrverse/Health}}. It spawns everywhere at a certain {{Florrverse/Rank}} in Ocean, depending on where it spawns. It spawns the most in the area linked to the entrance of Crab Kingdom. {{Florrverse/Mythic}}{{Florrverse/+}} Shells are quite tanky due to its high {{Florrverse/Health}} and shield, not to mention its pearl stats. Shells of the {{Florrverse/Ultra}} {{Florrverse/Rank}} are one of the most powerful {{Florrverse/Mob}}s of this {{Florrverse/Rank}}. They're tanky, damaging, and their shield makes them hard to kill. {{Florrverse/Flower}}s {{Florrverse/Common}}ly use Iris, Lightning, or other {{Florrverse/Petal}}s that deal Poison or Lightning {{Florrverse/Damage}} to override its armor. Pincer has the added benefit of slowing down the Shell, but because it only does this for 0.8 seconds, it's likely the Shell will stay im{{Florrverse/Mob}}ile for that time and not be affected.

Shell {{Florrverse/Drop}}s Shell, Magnet, and Pearl.

==== Shell ( {{Florrverse/Petal}}) ====
Shell consists of the {{Florrverse/Mob}} with the same name, but without the tail. Shell adds a shield to the {{Florrverse/User}} or allies. This shield is seen as a white bar covering the {{Florrverse/Health}} bar. Shield is depleted before {{Florrverse/Health}} does, which decays at a rate proportional to the amount of shield the {{Florrverse/User}} has.

These are strategies {{Florrverse/Flower}}s {{Florrverse/Common}}ly use:

* Shell's shield is too low to replace healing by itself, so it should be used in tandem with actual healing {{Florrverse/Petal}}s.
* Shell should not be used with Sponge given its insanely low shield per second rate.
* In many cases, it's outperformed by Amulet. This is why Shell is un{{Florrverse/Common}}.
* Since Shell can affect other {{Florrverse/Flower}}s near the {{Florrverse/User}}, so it can be helpful for group healing.

==== Pearl ====
Pearl is an un{{Florrverse/Common}} {{Florrverse/Petal}}. {{Florrverse/Flower}}s can control when it will throw its {{Florrverse/Petal}} away, and also in control, it will return to the {{Florrverse/Flower}}, hitting anything in its way. The Pearl is just like a Heavy, but instead of having black color, it is a faint yellow color, along with a darker color as the outline, and a white shine at the top right. This {{Florrverse/Petal}} works like Jelly, but has to be moved manually and it moves far from the {{Florrverse/Flower}} and possibly toss the {{Florrverse/Mob}} towards the {{Florrverse/Flower}}.

The Pearl has the same {{Florrverse/Health}} as rock, but it's not that good for survival as there is an additional delay for being thrown. In its thrown state, the pearl gets knocked back easily, meaning it will usually take a few seconds for it to deal the entirety of its {{Florrverse/Damage}}. Pearl is {{Florrverse/Common}}ly paired with the Talents of the {{Florrverse/Petal}} {{Florrverse/Health}} branch.

Pearl is one of the strongest PVP {{Florrverse/Petal}}s in the game. On {{Florrverse/Flower}}s, its dps far exceeds stinger. Pearl is great against stinger {{Florrverse/User}}s if the {{Florrverse/User}} also uses pollen, and it also does great {{Florrverse/Damage}} against summoner {{Florrverse/User}}s. Swapping Yin Yang continously can help {{Florrverse/Flower}}s aim better for their opponent, making the attack even more deadly. Most {{Florrverse/Flower}}s are unaware of the power that Pearls can bring, as it's an un{{Florrverse/Common}} strategy in the PvP area, which is Hel. This makes them useful for attacks that the targeted {{Florrverse/Flower}} doesn't have any time to react, making it a deadly {{Florrverse/Petal}} in PvP.

Pearl {{Florrverse/User}}s are {{Florrverse/Common}}ly defeated in PvP with {{Florrverse/Petal}}s that deal a high amount of {{Florrverse/Damage}} in a second, or generally {{Florrverse/Petal}}s that can deal more {{Florrverse/Damage}} and are able to do it faster. However, this is very, very, very difficult to do if they are using sponge. To successfully defeat them in this case, one must use an assassin build with bubbles and stingers, so that they can do a large amount of {{Florrverse/Damage}} in one strike, then quickly run away before they can catch the {{Florrverse/User}}.

Pearl has a base {{Florrverse/Health}} of 60 and a base {{Florrverse/Damage}} of 54, starting at the {{Florrverse/Unusual}} {{Florrverse/Rank}}.

=== Sponge ===
The sponge is a {{Florrverse/Mob}} in the {{Florrverse/Florrverse}}. It is stationary. It appears as a larger cartoonish smoke with circles grouped together with a pentagon shape. The edge is dark cream and the fill is cream. Sometimes, the {{Florrverse/Mob}} can be colored slightly purple. The pentagons are grouped together facing the same angle with every vertex and closely. There are three pentagons, making a total of 15 circles in the Sponge.

Strategy:

* Defeating Sponges are very easy due to its quite low {{Florrverse/Health}}, but it has some risks while trying to defeat it.
** The {{Florrverse/Mythic}} variants can be big to spawn in the narrow part, causing serious vibrations and can be fatal if the {{Florrverse/Flower}} trying to defeat it does not move away or use {{Florrverse/Petal}}s that rely on knockback.
** Also, If they have a {{Florrverse/Rank}} of {{Florrverse/Ultra}} or higher, they have enough {{Florrverse/Health}} to be annoying to defeat, allowing other {{Florrverse/Mob}}s plenty of time to kill the {{Florrverse/Flower}} trying to defeat the Sponge while fighting the it.
* This is used to escape hostile {{Florrverse/Mob}}s from defeating {{Florrverse/Flower}}s, but sometimes they may probably escape from the {{Florrverse/Mob}}.
* {{Florrverse/Ultra}} or {{Florrverse/Super}} Bone is an important {{Florrverse/Petal}} to clear multiple Sponges quickly, due to Sponges having low base {{Florrverse/Damage}} and Bone having good armor.

These are the strategies {{Florrverse/Flower}}s use for {{Florrverse/Super}} Sponges:

* The {{Florrverse/Super}} {{Florrverse/Mob}} itself isn't as dangerous, but the {{Florrverse/Ultra}} {{Florrverse/Mob}}s around it are a threat. When bubbling to the {{Florrverse/Mob}}, it is advised for {{Florrverse/Flower}}s to use sponge and multiple healing {{Florrverse/Petal}}s so that if anything hits the {{Florrverse/User}} of the bubbles, they don't die.
* If the Sponge spawns deep in ocean, it is advised for {{Florrverse/Flower}}s to form a "megasquad" so that {{Florrverse/Mob}}s can be cleared. It increases the chances of everyone surviving.
* When killing the Sponge, it is advised for {{Florrverse/Flower}}s to use sponge so that if a jellyfish deals lightning {{Florrverse/Damage}} or a Crab or leech randomly hits them, they won't die and be able to loot.
* {{Florrverse/Flower}}s {{Florrverse/Common}}ly use a high DPS ({{Florrverse/Damage}} per Second) build to secure the loot.

Sponges {{Florrverse/Drop}} Sponge and Coral.

==== Sponge ( {{Florrverse/Petal}}) ====
Sponge is a {{Florrverse/Petal}}. It absorbs {{Florrverse/Damage}} taken by {{Florrverse/User}}s. Similar to a cartoon style puff of smoke, but the inside is cream colored and the outline of it is much darker. It absorbs all of the {{Florrverse/Damage}} taken by the {{Florrverse/Flower}} and then slowly returns the absorbed {{Florrverse/Damage}} to the {{Florrverse/Flower}}. If the {{Florrverse/Petal}} is switched out before that, all remaining {{Florrverse/Damage}} it has absorbed is immediately dealt back to the {{Florrverse/Flower}}. Sponge is a somewhat difficult {{Florrverse/Petal}} to grind, due to there being no frequent {{Florrverse/Mythic}} sponge spawn area. It is advised that {{Florrverse/Flower}}s wait until they are set for {{Florrverse/Ultra}} Sponges.

It's best when combined with healing {{Florrverse/Petal}}s, as you will still take all the {{Florrverse/Damage}} the sponge absorbs. If the {{Florrverse/User}} uses powerful, consistent heals, like Starfish, you will be pretty much invincible. These heals must be combined with a basil or more to increase the healing. Sponge can be used with second chance to survive ramming high damaging {{Florrverse/Mob}}s multiple times.

Sponge goes extremely well with cotton, as it would still absorb the {{Florrverse/Damage}} sponge delays. 2 cotton of the same Rank makes the {{Florrverse/Flower}} hard to kill, especially with {{Florrverse/Reload}} talent. However, it does have a limit on how much {{Florrverse/Damage}} it can absorb.

Paired with Second Chance, the {{Florrverse/User}} can switch out, knowing that the {{Florrverse/Damage}} would cause eventual death even with the Sponge. All {{Florrverse/Damage}} will instantly be taken in, activating the talent and saving the {{Florrverse/Flower}} from any additional {{Florrverse/Damage}} after the duration of Second Chance.

==== Coral ====
Coral is a {{Florrverse/Petal}}. Its function is breaking upon impact and splitting into two pieces; each dealing half the original {{Florrverse/Damage}}.

Coral consists of a lavender piece of coral, arranged in a curvy 'Y' letter shape. Upon taking {{Florrverse/Damage}}, splits into smaller pieces (4 pieces maximum) that deal 50{{Florrverse/%}} of the {{Florrverse/Damage}} of the previous piece.

The half-{{Florrverse/Damage}} pieces can be split further into two even smaller pieces with each having a quarter of the original {{Florrverse/Damage}}.

Coral has the lowest HP stat of any {{Florrverse/Petal}} in the game at just 1, and one of the only to not increase with HP at higher rarities. Another {{Florrverse/Petal}} with this trait is Bubble.

=== Starfish ===
The Starfish is a {{Florrverse/Mob}} from the {{Florrverse/Florrverse}}. The Starfish is {{Florrverse/Unique}} , as it is one of the only enemies that have a defensive state, the other being the Moth. The Starfish has a similar look to its real-life counterpart. It is star-shaped, which means it has 5 limbs, and each limb has 3 little dots on it, summing up to 15 dots. When it takes a certain amount of {{Florrverse/Damage}}, it will start to lose some of its limbs. However, the limbs are regenerated when the Starfish is on low HP and is regenerating itself.

It has the same amount of speed as a {{Florrverse/Flower}}.

It has a {{Florrverse/Unique}} behaviour:

Starfish rotate and move around the map, until a target is in sight. When a target is found, the Starfish locks in, rotating faster and moving at a more moderate speed as they slam into {{Florrverse/Flower}}s. A {{Florrverse/Unique}} element to Starfish is that each time they lose some certain amount of {{Florrverse/Health}}, they also lose a random limb. When they lose a certain amount of limbs, Starfish flee and run away.

This defense mechanism can be countered by Powder, Wing, Bubble, and other {{Florrverse/Petal}}s. This also lets the Starfish regenerate {{Florrverse/Health}}, which allows them to re-enter fighting the target {{Florrverse/Flower}}. If they lose all of their {{Florrverse/Health}} regeneration from Dandelions, they will fight the {{Florrverse/Flower}} no matter how much {{Florrverse/Health}} the Starfish has.

The starfish can heal in its defensive state. However, if a Starfish gets hit by a dandelion, the starfish would go back to its attacking state as it can't heal. If no one brings at least one dandelion, {{Florrverse/Flower}}s can try to use death wheel builds to kill the starfish more quickly and efficiently. Other high {{Florrverse/Damage}} {{Florrverse/Petal}}s are good against Starfish since they {{Florrverse/Damage}} enough of their {{Florrverse/Health}} so they won't have any time to flee and regenerate.

{{Florrverse/Flower}}s usually don't use Dandelion against swarms of Starfishes of a certain {{Florrverse/Rank}}. {{Florrverse/Super}} Starfish have a normal aggressive speed. Because of this, {{Florrverse/Flower}}s are able to attack it from any side. They are aware if they attack from any side. If they attack from the front, they use certain {{Florrverse/Petal}}s so they don't get hit. If {{Florrverse/Flower}}s attack from the side (the actual side this time), they are aware if it changes direction and use long-range {{Florrverse/Petal}}s to combat it from a safe distance. If they attack it from behind, they are aware of the {{Florrverse/Health}} of the Starfish, and like if they are attacking from the side, they use long-range {{Florrverse/Petal}}s to combat it from a safe distance. Most {{Florrverse/Flower}}s bring Dandelions in {{Florrverse/Super}} Starfish combat.

In real life, Starfish could actually heal/regenerate their wounds if they lost one of their arms. However, the results were sometimes not perfect and the process time is far longer than in the {{Florrverse/Florrverse}}. The Starfish along with Desert Centipedes are the only {{Florrverse/Mob}}s that can {{Florrverse/Drop}} Salt, but even though Desert Centipedes have a higher {{Florrverse/Drop}} rate for Salt and more segments than Starfish, Starfish are much better to farm Salt as they have a much higher {{Florrverse/Mythic}} spawn rate.

Starfish {{Florrverse/Drop}} Salt and Starfish.

==== Starfish ( {{Florrverse/Petal}}) ====
Starfish is a {{Florrverse/Petal}} from the {{Florrverse/Florrverse}} derived from florr.io. It heals when its {{Florrverse/User}} has a {{Florrverse/Health}} below 75{{Florrverse/%}} of the maximum {{Florrverse/Health}} the {{Florrverse/Flower}} can have, not counting shield. The Starfish {{Florrverse/Petal}} is long and fairly skinny. It tapers slightly toward the top of the {{Florrverse/Petal}}. The tip is rounded. The {{Florrverse/Petal}} is red with a dark red outline and three pale red spots in the middle of the {{Florrverse/Petal}}. In general, it looks like one of the limbs of the {{Florrverse/Mob}}. It is good against many {{Florrverse/Mob}}s, because its healing is so fast but only when the {{Florrverse/Flower}} has 75{{Florrverse/%}} HP or below.

Starfish is the same as Yucca, except with the 75{{Florrverse/%}} modifier and it can heal if the {{Florrverse/Flower}} is not in its defensive position. Its appearance is also different.

== Species - Of Ant Hell ==
Ant Hell features a diverse array of species. There are many of them, with a few modifiers. The only external {{Florrverse/Mob}} is Worm. Since the Ants have similar stats, this section of this article will be relatively short.

=== Fire Ants ===
(All ants were mentioned in the {{Florrverse/Garden}} section)

==== Worker Fire Ants ====
Worker Fire Ants are the first Fire Ant type that doesn't spawn in Desert. It has the same speed and behaviour, and has the same appearance except that it is colored maroon. Just like the Worker Ant, it will wander around aimlessly until it is attacked, it will then become aggressive and start chasing the attacker until either, it dies, the attacker dies, or it loses sight of the attacker. Everything is the same as the Worker Ant although the {{Florrverse/Damage}} is twice as high.

The Worker Fire Ant spawns in the Ant Hell zone (the bottom left area), and also outside of it's spawn portal. {{Florrverse/Common}} and {{Florrverse/Unusual}} Worker Fire Ants can{{Florrverse/Rare}}ly spawn in the egg zone near the main exit portal. Worker Fire Ants have twice the body {{Florrverse/Damage}} as a normal worker ant.
