==== Queen Fire Ant ====
The Queen Fire Ant is a {{Florrverse/Mob}} in the {{Florrverse/Florrverse}} that is similar to Queen Ant, but slightly stronger. Unlike the Queen Ant, it doesn't spawn from Fire Ant Burrow, but only in Ant Hell. It has the same appearance as the Queen Ant, except that it is red instead of black.

It {{Florrverse/Drop}}s the same {{Florrverse/Drop}}s of the Queen Ant, Ant Egg and Basil.

==== Baby Fire Ant ====
Baby Fire Ants look like Baby Ants, only they are much more red in hue. It is passive on all rarities, but it becomes hostile if it spawns from a Fire Ant Egg. However, upon killing the {{Florrverse/Flower}} that spawned them, they become passive again.

Baby Fire Ant {{Florrverse/Drop}}s Light, Yucca, and Broccoli.

===== Broccoli =====
Broccoli looks like a floret of broccoli. Broccoli acts as a regular {{Florrverse/Petal}}, dealing {{Florrverse/Damage}} to an entity until its {{Florrverse/Health}} is depleted, after which the {{Florrverse/Petal}} explodes into three tiny projectiles.

The projectiles are spread out evenly, with a 120 degree gap between each one. The projectiles have random angles. The projectiles will never hit the {{Florrverse/Mob}} that landed the last hit on the Broccoli. Because of this, Broccoli is most effective in swarms.

It has a base {{Florrverse/Damage}} of 15 and Base {{Florrverse/Health}} of 10. By the way, Fire Ant Eggs are only a very slight red recolor of the Ant Egg, so it will be a section that might only be two lines long.

=== Termites ===

==== Worker Termite ====
The Worker Termite is a {{Florrverse/Mob}}. Exactly like the baby termite, but with an extra small circle at the back. This circle is smaller than the first but otherwise looks the same. The jaws move back and forth slightly if provoked. It has a psyonic connection with other termites, taking {{Florrverse/Damage}} if any other termites within a certain radius of itself takes {{Florrverse/Damage}}. Although semi-aggressive, this {{Florrverse/Mob}} is not threatening on its own but becomes deadly when paired with termite soldiers as they act as meatshields that keep the soldiers alive for longer. It has more {{Florrverse/Health}} compared to fire and normal ants and its psyonic connection makes it take even less {{Florrverse/Damage}} if there are other termites. Worker Termite {{Florrverse/Drop}}s Plank and Relic.

===== Plank =====
Plank looks similar to a wooden plank. It has a brown rectangular body with some scratches and a hole. Plank is a defensive {{Florrverse/Petal}}, meaning it cannot expand when attacking. If the {{Florrverse/Petal}} is hit by projectiles or other {{Florrverse/Flower}}s' {{Florrverse/Petal}}s in PvP, it will deal 20x its normal {{Florrverse/Damage}}.

These are the strategies {{Florrverse/Flower}}s use with Plank:

* Plank is useful in {{Florrverse/Garden}}, Jungle and Factory where projectile {{Florrverse/Mob}}s are present. Although Scorpions in Desert could be a reason to use Planks there, it is more advisable to use Lotuses instead.
** Plank can tank two projectile hits from Hornets, Mecha Wasps and Wasps of the same Rank, and five projectile hits from Mantises of the same {{Florrverse/Rank}} (except {{Florrverse/Super}} and {{Florrverse/Unique}} ). Since projectile {{Florrverse/Health}} scales exactly like {{Florrverse/Mob}} {{Florrverse/Health}}, Plank is vital to survival in high-Rank areas.
** Using two or three Planks spaced evenly should provide enough protection against projectiles.
* Plank could be used to fend off {{Florrverse/Petal}}s in Hel, but this usage is less {{Florrverse/Common}}.

===== Relic =====
Relic is a {{Florrverse/Petal}}. It spreads {{Florrverse/Damage}} taken by the {{Florrverse/Flower}} among others that also wear it and it also increases {{Florrverse/Flower}}s' max {{Florrverse/Health}}. The Relic looks like a brown star with a light brown interior and a slightly darker brown border. When equipped, it makes the {{Florrverse/Flower}} look more orange and does not circle the {{Florrverse/Flower}}, attaching to the {{Florrverse/Flower}}, like the Antennae. When equipped, the Relic will increase the {{Florrverse/Flower}}'s {{Florrverse/Health}} and spread the {{Florrverse/Damage}} (100{{Florrverse/%}} for all rarities) taken by the {{Florrverse/Flower}} to all {{Florrverse/Flower}}s (including the {{Florrverse/Flower}} that took the {{Florrverse/Damage}} first) with the Relic {{Florrverse/Petal}} equipped. It works only while it's equipped. {{Florrverse/Damage}} taken spreads around all the {{Florrverse/User}}s that have it equipped in their loadout.

This {{Florrverse/Petal}} is best used in teaming expeditions to prevent other team members from taking all of the {{Florrverse/Damage}}. The {{Florrverse/Damage}} can be neutralized if more {{Florrverse/Flower}}s who own this {{Florrverse/Petal}} actually use it alongside each other. Cotton can finish off the tiny bits of {{Florrverse/Damage}}.

==== Soldier Termite ====
Soldier Termite is a {{Florrverse/Mob}}. It's an aggresive {{Florrverse/Mob}} which chases the targeted {{Florrverse/Flower}} or summoned {{Florrverse/Mob}}s on sight, and it has Psyonic Connection, which will shares {{Florrverse/Damage}} taken among the Termites. It {{Florrverse/Drop}}s Bone and Mysterious Relic. It looks exactly like the worker termite but has two wings on its back. The wings are semi-transparent and look like white ovals attached to the back behind the head. The wings flap back and forth when aggressive but are still when passive.

It is slow when passive and medium when aggressive. It wanders around randomly, moving a few tiles before stopping and changing directions. Becomes aggressive when a {{Florrverse/Flower}} gets close, at which point it will the {{Florrverse/Flower}}. Its aggressive range is smaller than other aggressive {{Florrverse/Mob}}s like beetles and hornets, allowing you to get closer. Soldier ants also stop chasing you if the target {{Florrverse/Flower}} is at least a moderate distance away. It also has a psyonic connection with other termites.

Soldier Termites {{Florrverse/Drop}} Bone and Relic.

===== Bone =====
Bone consists of a typical, cartoonish portrait of a real-life bone's appearance: it is a vertically long and curved rectangle with heart-shaped figures in both ends of the {{Florrverse/Petal}}. Its color palette is white with gray edges surrounding it. Bone possesses the Armor attribute which reduces any physical {{Florrverse/Damage}} dealt to it by the Armor value, but loses half of its Armor each hit.

Bone is a good {{Florrverse/Petal}}, with powerful farming capabilities to {{Florrverse/Flower}}s. It has an Armor stat that reduces all {{Florrverse/Damage}} dealt to it by the Armor value. Each hit reduces its Armor by half.

==== Baby Termite ====
Baby termites are {{Florrverse/Mob}}s in the {{Florrverse/Florrverse}}. It moves around randomly for a few tiles before they change direction when passive, medium speed when aggressive, or rather spawned from an egg. It is weak and turns semi-aggressive when {{Florrverse/Health}} is under 50{{Florrverse/%}}. However, if it was spawned from a destroyed Termite Egg, or if a {{Florrverse/Flower}} {{Florrverse/Damage}}s any nearby Termite Egg, it will be aggressive towards the {{Florrverse/Flower}} who destroyed/attacked it. However, upon killing the {{Florrverse/Flower}} that spawned them, they become passive again. Every termite including this one has a psyonic connection. Although semi-aggressive when Termite Eggs are hit or otherwise passive, this {{Florrverse/Mob}} is not threatening on its own but becomes deadly when paired with termite soldiers as they act as meatshields that keep the soldiers alive for longer. It has more {{Florrverse/Health}} compared to fire and normal ants and its psyonic connection makes it take even less {{Florrverse/Damage}} if there are other termites so do not get overconfident and ram it.

Baby termites {{Florrverse/Drop}} Relic and Carrot.

===== Carrot =====
Carrot consists of a simple and cartoonish carrot appearance: it's an orange object with a cone-like appearance. Carrot also has green leaves sprouting out of its round end. Carrot, much like Missile, can be shot by going into attack position. However, it has a bonus feature compared to Missile: Carrot bounces when colliding with walls or {{Florrverse/Mob}}s. It deals less {{Florrverse/Damage}} than Missile, but it has more {{Florrverse/Health}} Points. When it gets near a wall, it changes direction right before hitting the wall rather than actually touching it and directly bouncing off. Carrot is built to be an alternative for Missile: it has more {{Florrverse/Health}} but deals less {{Florrverse/Damage}}, it can bounce off walls but it can be harder to farm them. They have their own pros and cons which need to be considered when choosing one or the other.

The Termite section of Ant Hell is a good place to farm for Carrots. They are crammed with Termites, including Baby Termites, where they {{Florrverse/Drop}} from. And since they are connected, it is very easy for a {{Florrverse/Flower}} to obtain a lot of Carrots at once, and even more if the {{Florrverse/Flower}} has a magnet. One must beware to not provoke Desert Centipedes without preparing oneself prior to aggroing the {{Florrverse/Mob}}, as they can spell a lot of trouble to you due to their speed. If they happen to burrow themselves and reaggro, it will be better for the {{Florrverse/Flower}}. Carrot is very good in farming bubbles, which is like a loop. {{Florrverse/Flower}}s can farm bubbles, get to high {{Florrverse/Rank}}ed Termites faster, get higher {{Florrverse/Rank}}ed Carrots, go back to the Ocean, and get higher {{Florrverse/Rank}}ed Bubbles. Carrot is very useful, and its usefulness is pretty trivial, especially in enclosed spots that have the least {{Florrverse/Mob}} densities, and in open spaces with only some walls.

==== Termite Overmind ====
(Please don't use this information in a "yo mama" roast.) The Termite Overmind is the largest {{Florrverse/Mob}} in the {{Florrverse/Florrverse}}. It is over five times the size of a Baby Ant of the same {{Florrverse/Rank}}. It looks much like a Baby Termite, but a lot (5x) larger. The pincers at the front are also more curved inward compared to that of a Baby Ant. Due to this, it is very slow. Literally. VERY slow. It is passive until it is attacked either directly or spread across other Termites via connection. It will lock on the nearest {{Florrverse/Flower}} and move toward them very slowly. It tends to rotate clockwise. Like other termites, it has a psyonic connection that shares {{Florrverse/Damage}} with termites. {{Florrverse/Super}} Termite Overminds can disable slots of {{Florrverse/Flower}}s randomly, making any {{Florrverse/Petal}} in the disabled slot inactive for a period of time. It can disable up to 7 of the slots of one {{Florrverse/Flower}} at once.

The Overmind has a lot of {{Florrverse/Health}} compared to all other {{Florrverse/Mob}}s of the {{Florrverse/Ultra}} {{Florrverse/Rank}} but is very slow as compensation. If any termites or Worms spawn nearby, {{Florrverse/Flower}}s tend to take them out as fast as possible to as the real danger when fighting the Overmind are Soldier Termites sharing their {{Florrverse/Damage}} with the Overmind and overwhelming {{Florrverse/Flower}}s. Worms are also a threat because they are fast and always burrow underground. It {{Florrverse/Drop}}s Tomato, Relic, and Compass.

===== Tomato =====
Tomato is a {{Florrverse/Petal}} from the {{Florrverse/Florrverse}}. It can increase in size and {{Florrverse/Damage}}. In other words, the bigger its size is, the more {{Florrverse/Damage}} it does. Its {{Florrverse/Health}} always stays the same no matter the size. It looks like a tomato (obviously). Has a red round body with green calyx on top.

If {{Florrverse/Flower}}s have enough Tomatoes, then it can be useful for surviving with them dealing {{Florrverse/Damage}} in an ascending order. Both the {{Florrverse/Reload}} stats benefit from skills. It can be used to kill stronger {{Florrverse/Mob}}s if {{Florrverse/Flower}}s have weak {{Florrverse/Petal}}s and {{Florrverse/Ultra}}-{{Florrverse/Super}}s if used well with the right rotation speed. As the hitbox size increases with {{Florrverse/Damage}}, it can be utilized to block {{Florrverse/Petal}}s/projectiles.

High tier tomatoes, unlike stinger, it can be used to multi-hit enemies, which can prove to be overpowered. Most tomato {{Florrverse/User}}s already have a bone of the same level, which limits its potential. Still, it is a deadly force against most {{Florrverse/Mob}}s and usually out classes bone due to powerful burst dmg.

Without {{Florrverse/Ultra}} {{Florrverse/Reload}} talent, Tomato is stronger than Stinger if both break in the same amount of hits, but it will be outclassed after you obtain {{Florrverse/Ultra}} {{Florrverse/Reload}} Talent due to the 3 second growing time being unaffected.

===== Compass =====
Compass is a special {{Florrverse/Petal}} from the {{Florrverse/Florrverse}}. It points to the nearest {{Florrverse/Mob}} of the {{Florrverse/Super}} {{Florrverse/Rank}} or higher or to the nearest Square {{Florrverse/Mob}} of any {{Florrverse/Rank}}. Its appearance depicts a generic compass without North and South on it: it is a circle with a blue fill and a gray outline. It has two arrows representing the needles in a real-life compass, colored white and red. Broken compasses have a gray fill and a large, light gray crack on the left. Compass tracks and points to the nearest {{Florrverse/Super}} {{Florrverse/+}} {{Florrverse/Mob}} or Square {{Florrverse/Mob}} of any Rank (exclusive to {{Florrverse/Unique}} and {{Florrverse/Eternal}} Compasses) relative to the {{Florrverse/User}}’s current location. When no {{Florrverse/Super}} {{Florrverse/+}} {{Florrverse/Mob}} or Square {{Florrverse/Mob}} is present, Compass keeps refreshing, with the needle pointing to a random direction each time it refreshes.

For this only reason, Compass is extremely {{Florrverse/Common}} across very experienced {{Florrverse/Flower}}s. Also, Compasses of the {{Florrverse/Mythic}} {{Florrverse/Rank}} or lower are broken, making them effectively useless and only used as decoy. Magnets disturb compasses.

=== Worm ===
The Worm looks like a brown circle with triangular shaped teeth on it. Its teeth are placed randomly on its mouth. When burrowed, its body elongates into a larger body, much like Leech: however, the entire structure lies underground, like Desert Centipede or a {{Florrverse/Flower}} using Shovel to burrow underground. Worm is an aggressive {{Florrverse/Mob}} which stays underground as if it were using a Shovel until it sees a {{Florrverse/Flower}}. It then chases the {{Florrverse/Flower}} until it is underneath it, then pops up, dealing extreme {{Florrverse/Damage}}.

{{Florrverse/Super}}{{Florrverse/+}} Worms can swallow {{Florrverse/Flower}}s, teleporting them inside of the worm, where they will need to kill the {{Florrverse/Super}} {{Florrverse/+}} Worm by attacking the Worm Guts to leave. Worm Guts don't break, which means that they do not {{Florrverse/Drop}} any {{Florrverse/Petal}}s, and {{Florrverse/Damage}} dealt to them will be transferred to the Worm's {{Florrverse/Health}}. Damaging Worm Guts increases the chances of you receiving loot, because it counts as {{Florrverse/Damage}} to the Worm. While inside the Worm, everyone takes immense poison {{Florrverse/Damage}}.

Worm {{Florrverse/Drop}}s Shovel and Soil.

==== Shovel ====
While underground, the {{Florrverse/Flower}} will be immune to all kinds of {{Florrverse/Damage}} (except for worm or desert centipede while burrowed) and can pass through entities. The {{Florrverse/Flower}} will be shown as a dark grey dot and their movement speed will be decreased (while underground). Soil affects the size of the dark grey dot. Magnets will stop working, but Antennae will still work like usual and the {{Florrverse/Flower}} can pick up {{Florrverse/Petal}}s by touching them.

==== Soil ====
Soil is a brown heptagon. It makes the {{Florrverse/User}} larger and increases their {{Florrverse/Health}} when equipped. (This section is short for external reasons)

== Species - of The Jungle ==

=== Bush ===
Bush consists of a green star with rounded edges, along with a dark green snowflake inside of it. It is stationary. It {{Florrverse/Drop}}s Golden Leaf, Magic Leaf, and Monstera.

==== Golden Leaf ====
Golden Leaf looks like Leaf, but is recolored to look (as the name suggests) golden. Golden Leaf's special ability is reducing the {{Florrverse/Reload}} time of all {{Florrverse/Petal}}s in the loadout, which stacks multiplicatively. For example, using two {{Florrverse/Ultra}} Golden Leaves reduces {{Florrverse/Petal}} {{Florrverse/Reload}} by 1 - (1 - 17.5{{Florrverse/%}})<sup>2</sup> ≈ 31.9{{Florrverse/%}}.

==== Magic Leaf ====
Magic Leaf is a {{Florrverse/Petal}} from the {{Florrverse/Florrverse}}. It acts like a normal Leaf, but generates Mana passively instead of healing the {{Florrverse/User}}. Magic Leaf is {{Florrverse/Drop}}ped by others that {{Florrverse/Drop}} leaves and Bush with an orb equipped. Magic Leaf looks like the original Leaf, but with a cyan color and a darker cyan outline. Magic Leaf functions like a normal Leaf, but generates Mana passively instead of healing, and grants the Base Max Mana attribute, allowing Mana to be generated, stored and consumed.

==== Monstera ====
Monstera is a {{Florrverse/Petal}} from the {{Florrverse/Florrverse}}. It heals the {{Florrverse/User}} and {{Florrverse/Flower}}s around them passively, the effect depends on the distance from the {{Florrverse/Petal}}. Monstera is {{Florrverse/Drop}}ped by Bush. Monstera has a similar shape of a Leaf with a bigger body and creases along the edges. Monstera allows {{Florrverse/Flower}}s to heal {{Florrverse/Flower}}s around them (including the {{Florrverse/User}}) in a certain area. The effect depends on the distance to the {{Florrverse/Petal}}.

=== Jungle Centipede ===
Body segments consist of a purple circle with a slightly darker outline. On opposite sides of the circle, the tips of two small, black circles show, representing legs. The segment moves perpendicular to the direction the legs are oriented. Its head is exactly like the body, but has two antennae that point in the direction it's moving. The antennae consist of a small, curved, black line with a small, black circle at the end. The antennae appear on both sides of the head and point away from the center.

All segments move forward with the front-most segment, and the front-most segment moves toward the {{Florrverse/Flower}} while targeting it.

The Centipede is able to collide with its own body, meaning that the centipede gets tangled up in its own body, impeding its movement.

If a middle segment is destroyed, the front most segment in the new set of segments becomes a head (though it still looks like a body segment).

It {{Florrverse/Drop}}s Iris and Grapes.

==== Grapes ====
Grapes consists of a purple-colored version of Peas, with four small Peas (or Grapes) composing it. The number can increase to 6 with the Duplicator Talent. Grapes function exactly like Peas, but as their description implies, they deal poison {{Florrverse/Damage}}, much like Iris, at the cost of dealing less physical {{Florrverse/Damage}}. Grapes are like a stronger version of Peas.

=== Firefly ===
The Firefly is a {{Florrverse/Mob}} from the {{Florrverse/Florrverse}}. The front of the {{Florrverse/Mob}} is almost identical to that of the Fly, whilst its back, composed out of a glowing yellow circle, with a line. It is slower than the Fly, but moves in the exact same way. It is neutral, meaning if it is left alone, it is passive, and if it gets {{Florrverse/Damage}}d, then it turns aggressive. Their back glows, as well as they are to emit lightning, that chains upon {{Florrverse/Flower}}s.

It doesn't pose a threat, because it has low {{Florrverse/Health}} and it's slower than the {{Florrverse/Flower}}. It is advised to not ram it, if {{Florrverse/Flower}}s don't want to risk to get exposed to the effect similar to the battery. With higher rarities, summons are extremely dangerous to use because of all of the lightning {{Florrverse/Flower}}s will have to endure. To get around this, {{Florrverse/Flower}}s use a lot of high Rank Ant Eggs so you have enough summons not to be included in the Lightning bounce. Or, Rubber also works.

Fireflies {{Florrverse/Drop}} Wing, Bulb, and Battery.

==== Wing ====
It is a white crescent with a light gray outline. It constantly rotates around its center while simultaneously revolving around the {{Florrverse/Flower}}. When attacking it moves outward very far, then back to the normal attack distance. This movement effectively gives the {{Florrverse/Petal}} more range. This makes the {{Florrverse/Petal}} very useful against ranged {{Florrverse/Mob}}s like Hornets, especially when combined with Third Eye. This combo also can be used to hit {{Florrverse/Mob}}s through walls.

Its key advantage is its long range, which means it can attack {{Florrverse/Mob}}s from a safe distance. However, Wing is hard to use.

==== Bulb ====
Light Bulb consists of a cartoonish lightbulb appearance: it is circular with a dark gray handle with even darker borders. The lightbulb is yellow-colored, indicating that it's emitting light, and there are white lines zigzagging around inside the lightbulb, starting and ending on the base. During usage, Light Bulb will emit a yellow glow around its center, constantly increasing and decreasing in radius, bearing the same radius as Uranium's green glow.

Light Bulb serves to attract {{Florrverse/Mob}}s that are in a certain radius from the {{Florrverse/Petal}}. The effect radius is dependent on Light Bulb's Rank. Attracted {{Florrverse/Mob}}s will then follow you. It is able to provoke neutral and aggressive {{Florrverse/Mob}}s, but it can't attract passive, non-sentient or stationary ones like Bubble {{Florrverse/Mob}}, Cactus {{Florrverse/Mob}} or Sandstorm. The aggro effect doesn't stack, meaning using more Bulbs won't aggro {{Florrverse/Mob}}s from further away. The aggro range pull works independently from the glow that Light Bulb emits, as the glow is only a visual effect.

==== Battery ====
Battery consists of a cartoonish battery appearance: it is a large rectangle, with orange and black color palettes. The black part takes around 75{{Florrverse/%}} of the rectangle, while the orange part takes 25{{Florrverse/%}} of it. It has a smaller silver rectangle attached to the top of the orange section, indicating its charger hole.

Whenever the {{Florrverse/Flower}} makes contact with a {{Florrverse/Mob}} or another {{Florrverse/Flower}}, Battery will release a total of three lightning discharges at once to the closest enemy to the {{Florrverse/Flower}}, bouncing a set amount of entities per Rank. The lightning that's discharged acts similarly to Lightning's electrical discharges. Think of it like a Cutter but with Lightning.

==== Magic Firefly ====
Magic Fireflies are a cyan recolored version of Firefly and they emit a blue glow instead of a yellow one. Magic Fireflies spawn in waves, with each wave lasting 3 minutes. During the wave, magic fireflies spawn everywhere except the top left of Jungle (near ocean portal). After a wave ends, another wave will appear randomly within the next three hours. This sometimes makes it harder to get for newer {{Florrverse/Flower}}s with lesser time on their hands. Magic Fireflies don't pose a major threat, because they have low {{Florrverse/Health}} and are slower than the {{Florrverse/Flower}}. It is advised that {{Florrverse/Flower}}s do not ram the Magic Firefly, as ramming causes it to discharge large amounts of lightning {{Florrverse/Damage}}. With higher rarities, summons are extremely dangerous to use against all Firefly variants. All Magic Firefly rarities spawn with intervals of randomized minutes in between, so it is advised for {{Florrverse/Flower}}s not to wait for the next wave straight after the last. Additionally, Magic Fireflies can only spawn if the {{Florrverse/Mob}} density is low enough: this means that if there are too many {{Florrverse/Mob}}s, higher Rank Magic Fireflies cannot spawn. The best strategy to farm them is to use Bubble and Uranium around the Firefly zone which can usually guarantee{{Florrverse/Rare}} and {{Florrverse/Epic}} Mana Orbs. For more experienced {{Florrverse/Flower}}s, Bubble around the {{Florrverse/Mythic}} zone with {{Florrverse/Petal}}s that multihit like corn, they do high {{Florrverse/Damage}} like claw, or with a good squad. Magic Fireflies are often greeded. To get around this, {{Florrverse/Flower}}s go to areas {{Florrverse/Flower}}s don't normally visit, such as the right edge of the right side of Jungle or the Wasp zone. Doing this should find {{Florrverse/Flower}}s a few more than they otherwise would normally find. Magic Fireflies {{Florrverse/Drop}} Orb and Battery.

===== Orb =====
Orb consists of a cyan circle with a darker outline, similar to the color of Lightning. When equipped, Orb adds an attribute called base mana (which causes the mana bar to appear) to the {{Florrverse/User}}, allowing mana to be generated, stored and consumed. Orb is consumed by the {{Florrverse/User}} like Rose, granting a fixed amount of mana until the mana bar is full. it also allows the {{Florrverse/User}} to find magic {{Florrverse/Petal}}s, which are only accessible through the {{Florrverse/Petal}}. There are some {{Florrverse/Petal}}s selected to have their magic variants, including: Peas and Grapes -> Blueberries, Bubble -> Magic Bubble, Cactus -> Magic Cactus, Cotton -> Magic Cotton, all Leaf variants -> Magic Leaf, Third Eye -> Magic Eye, all Missile variants -> Magic Missile, Mysterious Stick -> Magic Stick, Rose -> Mana Orb, Stinger and its blood counterpart -> Magic Stinger.

=== Jungle Ladybug ===
Jungle Ladybugs are {{Florrverse/Mob}}s in the {{Florrverse/Florrverse}} derived from florr.io. The Jungle variant of Ladybugs look like Ladybugs with a darker fill and lighter spots. It's best for {{Florrverse/Flower}}s to attack this one when they are clear of any aggressive {{Florrverse/Mob}}s which are nearby. These aren't much of a threat though, with a lower body {{Florrverse/Damage}} than Leafbug so that even if one gets pushed into one of these by enemy projectiles they wouldn't take much {{Florrverse/Damage}}. The best counter is using Bone of a higher Rank to attack. Jungle Ladybugs {{Florrverse/Drop}} Dahlia and Yin Yang.

==== Yin Yang ====
Yin Yang is a {{Florrverse/Petal}}. They change the direction of the {{Florrverse/Flower}}'s {{Florrverse/Petal}} orbit. Appears like a Yin Yang with the two dots missing. The center has a sharper turn than a standard yin yang. Yin Yangs rotate around their center as well as revolving around the {{Florrverse/Flower}}.

Equipping Yin Yangs changes the direction that the {{Florrverse/User}}'s {{Florrverse/Petal}}s rotate, and the placement of {{Florrverse/Petal}}s. Even amounts of Yin Yangs make {{Florrverse/Petal}}s spin clockwise, and odd amounts make them spin counterclockwise.

With more Yin Yangs higher than 2, the {{Florrverse/User}}'s {{Florrverse/Petal}}s will start to layer on top of other {{Florrverse/Petal}}, making it seems to gain additional length. The way it works is that every 2nth Yin Yang increases the minimum layer each {{Florrverse/Petal}}s column must have by 1. Each column can't have less than the minimum number of {{Florrverse/Petal}}s and any remaining {{Florrverse/Petal}}s that couldn't form a column will instead added and distributed to existing columns until there's enough number of remaining {{Florrverse/Petal}}s to create a new column.

For example: With 6 Yin Yangs (3 minimum layers on each column), the 6 {{Florrverse/Petal}}s will form 2 '3 {{Florrverse/Petal}}s' columns. Adding a 7th {{Florrverse/Petal}} will stack it on one of the column, thus one of the column will have 4 {{Florrverse/Petal}}s, and adding an 8th {{Florrverse/Petal}} will stack it on the next column, thus both columns have 4 {{Florrverse/Petal}}s. Finally, adding a 9th {{Florrverse/Petal}} will make the 7th and 8th {{Florrverse/Petal}}s that once can't form a column to now form a new column of 3 {{Florrverse/Petal}}s with the 9th {{Florrverse/Petal}}. This process is repeated for the 10th, 11th, and so on.

Odd numbers of Yin Yangs make the {{Florrverse/Petal}}s rotate along with other {{Florrverse/Petal}}s instead of against so it reduces attack but increases defense. 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10 Yin Yangs extend some {{Florrverse/Petal}}s into orbits further away from the {{Florrverse/Flower}} so it is good for range.

The main purpose of Yin Yangs, especially with the new world map, is to travel quickly between maps. Rapidly swapping a {{Florrverse/Petal}} with a Yin Yang causes your {{Florrverse/Petal}}s to switch back and forth between rotating counterclockwise and clockwise. When paired with Bubbles, this allows the {{Florrverse/User}} to boost forward without having to wait for the bubbles to revolve back into position again.

=== Leafbug ===
The Leafbug uses a similar body to the Scorpion except its body is changed into a leaf, and has eight legs instead of six and uses the pincers from Beetle. Leafbugs have a much higher armor than all {{Florrverse/Mob}}s, making them able to defeat {{Florrverse/Flower}}s easier than normally with other {{Florrverse/Mob}}s. Leafbugs {{Florrverse/Drop}} Leaf and Root.

==== Root ====
Root is a {{Florrverse/Petal}} from the {{Florrverse/Florrverse}}. It gives the {{Florrverse/User}} a layer of Armor each second with a capacity of 10 layers. One layer is removed every time the {{Florrverse/Flower}} takes physical {{Florrverse/Damage}}. It is brown like the stick, with the shape of a simple mountain which has bumps. Root gives the {{Florrverse/User}} a layer of armor every second until the limit of 10 layers is reached, and one layer is removed whenever the {{Florrverse/User}} receives physical {{Florrverse/Damage}}. For example, if a {{Florrverse/Flower}} is using a {{Florrverse/Mythic}} Root and has accumulated 10 layers of armor, then the {{Florrverse/User}} possesses 607.5 × 10 = 6,075 armor. When the {{Florrverse/User}} hits an {{Florrverse/Ultra}} Soldier Ant, which does 7,290 physical {{Florrverse/Damage}}, then the {{Florrverse/User}} receives 7,290 - 6,075 = 1,215 physical {{Florrverse/Damage}}, and a layer of armor is removed, leaving the {{Florrverse/User}} with 6,075 - 607.5 = 5,467.5 armor.

==== Golden Leafbug ====
The golden leafbug is a {{Florrverse/Rare}} variant of the Leafbug. The Golden Leafbug looks like a regular Leafbug, with its colors switched to be golden. It {{Florrverse/Drop}}s Golden Leaf and Root.

=== Mantis ===
Mantis consists of a green oval with a "stick"-like shape as a pattern. It has the same antennae as Hornet, but larger. (It does not {{Florrverse/Drop}} Antennae, however) Also, it has 6 legs that move around when it moves. It is aggressive, and it will shoot missiles at its targets. The Peas inflict an armor debuff, which lowers the amount of armor the {{Florrverse/Flower}} hit has. The Mantis is slower than {{Florrverse/Flower}}s, so they can maintain a distance without needing any speed-boosting {{Florrverse/Petal}}s. The missiles it shoots are slower than the missiles of Hornets, so they should be easy to dodge. However, the Mantis shoots three of them at a time.

Alone, a single Mantis isn't a threat because, as mentioned above, its projectiles are easy to dodge. However, with two Mantises or more, or a Mantis along with a {{Florrverse/Mob}} or many {{Florrverse/Mob}}s, they will become potential supporter {{Florrverse/Mob}}s, even if they accompany lower Rank {{Florrverse/Mob}}s. {{Florrverse/Flower}}s pile on Leafbugs, neutral {{Florrverse/Mob}}s with high body {{Florrverse/Damage}}, as they could easily be knocked or forced into, and Fireflies, weak but damaging {{Florrverse/Mob}}s that often fly into them, and Bushes, which, like Leafbugs, they can easily be knocked or forced into, but also can straight-up block their path completely. Mantis {{Florrverse/Drop}}s Bur and Peas.

==== Bur ====
Bur consists of a small {{Florrverse/Petal}}, with a blood red color and dark red outlines. The {{Florrverse/Petal}}'s shape is similar to Lightning; however, Lightning is cyan, the spikes on it have are pointy and it has ten sides, while Bur is crimson, its "spikes" are actually semi-circles and there are twelve semi-circles. Once Bur hits an enemy, it will deal its base {{Florrverse/Damage}} and an effect called Armor Deebuff. This effect decreases the Armor statistic of the enemy by the listed number depending on the {{Florrverse/Rank}}. For comparison, {{Florrverse/Ultra}} Leafbug has 7,873 Armor, and {{Florrverse/Ultra}} Bur reduces it by 1,093.5, which means {{Florrverse/Ultra}} Leafbug will have 7,873 - 1,093.5 = 6,779.5 Armor remaining after being debuffed. If the Armor debuffed is more than the Armor value, then the Armor is able to wander into negative values, and, instead of the Armor subtracting {{Florrverse/Damage}} by its value, it will be a double negative: the Armor will begin adding {{Florrverse/Damage}} to every hit on the {{Florrverse/Mob}} (e.g. if a {{Florrverse/Mob}} has a -200 Armor value due to Bur's effects and a {{Florrverse/Common}} Basic which has 10 {{Florrverse/Damage}} hits the debuffed {{Florrverse/Mob}}, the final {{Florrverse/Damage}} would be 10 - (-200) = 210, which the {{Florrverse/Mob}} suffers from the {{Florrverse/Common}} Basic). This effect can't be stacked and only lasts for 3 seconds.

=== Termite Mound ===
It appears as a faded light brown variant of an Ant Hole. Its {{Florrverse/Health}}bar is yellow due to it not being able to be {{Florrverse/Damage}}d directly. The Termite Mound spawns in Jungle as a {{Florrverse/Rare}} spawn. It spawns more frequently in the corridors branching out from the bottom, opposite to the Ant Hell portal. Termite mounds {{Florrverse/Drop}} Relic, Soil, and Rubber. {{Florrverse/Flower}}s can enter it and defeat the termites inside. It dies when all the Termites inside get defeated.

==== Rubber ====
It is a square with curved sides, resembling a marshmallow. The {{Florrverse/Petal}} uses the same colors as Basic. Rubber increases knockback received from all collisions (except collision with other {{Florrverse/Flower}}s) and is stackable. The increased knockback will still apply if the {{Florrverse/Petal}} is broken. Rubber also absorbs {{Florrverse/Damage}} from lightning until it has no {{Florrverse/Health}}, and any excess {{Florrverse/Damage}} will be dealt to the {{Florrverse/User}} of the Rubber.

=== Wasp ===
Wasps looks like a Hornet but it has many differences: its Antennae are larger, its body is colored orange and it has 2 stripes on its body instead of usual 3. The stripes are slightly curved and are larger. It has the same speed and behavior as Hornets. The Wasp is essentially a Hornet with rapid fire (doubled fire rate), a wider Missile, and a curving wave pattern (Wasp missiles move similarly to Bees). Also, it's {{Florrverse/Drop}} rates for Missile and Antennae are better than Hornet {{Florrverse/Drop}} rates, however not {{Florrverse/Drop}}ping Orange, instead {{Florrverse/Drop}}ping Blood Stinger) It {{Florrverse/Drop}}s Blood Stinger, Antennae and Missile.

==== Blood Stinger ====
Its appearance is nearly identical to that of Stinger, but instead the {{Florrverse/Petal}} uses a more reddish tint. It also appears that the edges of the {{Florrverse/Petal}} curve inward, much like a Trap in the Arrasverse. Its base {{Florrverse/Reload}} time is 7.5s, or 75{{Florrverse/%}} of Stinger's {{Florrverse/Reload}} time. It functions like Stinger but deals a certain amount of {{Florrverse/Damage}} to the {{Florrverse/Flower}} upon spawning. It cannot lower the {{Florrverse/User}}'s HP below 1.

== Species - of Hel ==
Hel is an area in the {{Florrverse/Florrverse}}. It is the only area that has all of its {{Florrverse/Mob}}s exclusive to it. This area has PvP.

=== Hel Beetles ===
It looks like a regular Beetle, except that it is dark red in color and is a little bigger than a normal Beetle. The pincers on the front are replaced with a realistic mouth with five sharp black teeth that move around slightly. It remains passive until stopping a {{Florrverse/Flower}}. Once it spots the {{Florrverse/Flower}}, the Beetle will chase the {{Florrverse/Flower}}. It can also teleport.

The Hel Beetle is hard to defeat due to its fast movement speed, high HP, high body {{Florrverse/Damage}}, and ability to teleport directly on top of you. {{Florrverse/Flower}}s should use {{Florrverse/Petal}}s that can slow down {{Florrverse/Mob}}s, such as Web, Pincer, Heavy, and {{Florrverse/Mythic}}{{Florrverse/+}} Jelly (not very advised to use Jelly as it has little knockback against{{Florrverse/Legendary}}{{Florrverse/+}} Hel Beetles). When fighting Hel Beetles, {{Florrverse/Flower}}s need to be vigilant of other {{Florrverse/Flower}}s, since Hel is a PvP zone. On top of that, they also have to be wary of running into large groups of Hel beetles, since in swarms, they can easily overwhelm and kill a {{Florrverse/Flower}} and also can't be slowed down, as Hel Beetles behind push them forwards. {{Florrverse/Mythic}}{{Florrverse/+}} Rubber is also useful as it can provide knockback and prevent multiple hits from a Hel Beetle. Since Hel is a PVP zone, it is advised for {{Florrverse/Flower}}s to use Sponge, which can prevent them from dying instantly to other {{Florrverse/Flower}}s.

Hel Beetles {{Florrverse/Drop}} Mark, Beetle Egg, and Dice.

==== Mark ====
The Mark appears to bear a dark red color with even darker borders. The shape of this {{Florrverse/Petal}} is a pentagram: a five-pointed regular star with a regular pentagon in the star's central area. The Mark sends every dead {{Florrverse/Flower}} it touches to Hel after a certain time, depending on the Rank. The Mark affects dead {{Florrverse/Flower}}s in Hel similar to how it would in other areas, sending the marked {{Florrverse/Flower}} back to Hel. Mark has an extra hidden mechanic in which it functions like Yggdrasil when the dead {{Florrverse/Flower}} is already in Hel, but instead of reviving the {{Florrverse/Flower}}, it teleports them to a random spot on the map and then revives them.

==== Dice ====
Dice appears as a white square with gray borders and a number of pips inside, which varies between 1-6 pips at a fixed interval. When changing, the number of pips will twitch and circle before changing to another number of pips (e.g., from 3 to 4). If the game rolls the same number of pips twice, Dice won't change appearance nor the pip number will twitch and circle, and a new pip number will happen in the next interval as usual. In case you didn't know, 1 pip appears as a single circle in the centre. 2 pips appear as two circles at opposite corners. 3 pips appear the same as 2 pips, except that there is also a pip in the centre. 4 pips appear the same as 2 pips, except that there is a pip for every corner. 5 pips appear the same as 4 pips, except that there is a pip in the centre like 1 pip and 3 pips. Lastly, 6 pips appear the same as 4 pips, except that there are two extra pips on opposing sides.

Dice has the same stats as Basic and a 5{{Florrverse/%}} base chance to deal 35 times its base {{Florrverse/Damage}}. For each point in luck, which can be increased by Clover and the Luck talent, the chance increases by 4{{Florrverse/%}}. For example, with Eternal Luck talent and {{Florrverse/Super}} Clover, Dice has a 5{{Florrverse/%}} {{Florrverse/+}} (2.7 {{Florrverse/+}} 0.8) × 4{{Florrverse/%}} = 19{{Florrverse/%}} chance to land a critical hit.

=== Hel Centipede ===
(There are FOUR centipede variants now)

It appears the same as a Centipede, except that it is dark red. It has shorter {{Florrverse/Damage}}d Antennae and unevenly sized segments. Some segments even have what appears to be bites taken out of them.

{{Florrverse/Flower}}s {{Florrverse/Common}}ly use Lightning against this {{Florrverse/Mob}}. This is because the lightning will chain upon multiple segments of the centipede. Batteries have lightning {{Florrverse/Damage}}, but they are not recommended due to the Centipede's high body {{Florrverse/Damage}}. Hel centipedes {{Florrverse/Drop}} Marks and Dominoes.

==== Domino ====
Domino appears as a rectangular tile with rounded corners, dark gray pips and a line through the middle, resembling a domino in real life. It appears as two dice combined and fused together in the most orderly stack possible. There is a border separating the two, but it doesn't extend entirely to the domino's edges.

Domino deals {{Florrverse/Damage}} based on the product of pips shown on each end, ranging from 0 (no pips shown) to 6 pips. For example, if a Domino has 2 pips on one end and 5 pips on the other, it will deal 2 × 5 = 10 times its base {{Florrverse/Damage}}. Excluding duplicate cases, Domino has 28 possible combinations of pips, with each having a 1/28 chance to show up, and does 9.5x its base {{Florrverse/Damage}} on average. There are 7 cases without any duplicates: 0 and 0, 1 and 1, 2 and 2, 3 and 3, 4 and 4, 5 and 5, and 6 and 6. Every other case has a duplicate case with it.

=== Hel Spider ===
The Hel Spider appears as a Spider, but it is slightly red and has the Hel Beetle's mouth. Hel Spider acts just like a regular spider, but has 2.4x the {{Florrverse/Health}} and 2x poison {{Florrverse/Damage}}. It also has 2.67 seconds of poison duration instead of 2 seconds like the normal Spider. {{Florrverse/Flower}}s counteract this by using Lotus to reduce the poison dealed by the Spider. It {{Florrverse/Drop}}s Mark, Card, and Third Eye, but still very{{Florrverse/Rare}}ly.

==== Card ====
Card consists of a white rectangle with a gray border, two "A"s on the top left and bottom right corners of the rectangle (whereas the bottom right one is upside down) and a symbol in the middle, which varies depending on the suit, resembling a real-life card. It can be a black spade (♠️), a black club (♣️), a red heart (♥️) and a red diamond (♦️). The "A"s are black on spades and clubs, and red on hearts and diamonds. Spade's base {{Florrverse/Health}} is 270, and its base {{Florrverse/Damage}} is 45. This {{Florrverse/Petal}} starts at the{{Florrverse/Rare}} rank. Club's base {{Florrverse/Health}} at{{Florrverse/Rare}} is 225 and its base {{Florrverse/Damage}} is 90. Heart's base {{Florrverse/Health}} at{{Florrverse/Rare}} is 180 and its base {{Florrverse/Damage}} also at{{Florrverse/Rare}} is 135. Diamond, has the sharpest corners of all of the shapes. And realistically, it has the least {{Florrverse/Health}} out of the four, like a Stinger of its kind, which is 135, and its base {{Florrverse/Damage}} which is the highest, also like a Stinger of its kind, is 180.

At first glance, Card is a pretty simple {{Florrverse/Petal}}, dealing {{Florrverse/Damage}} just as a normal {{Florrverse/Petal}} would do, like Basic. However, once it dies, it is able to respawn into one of its four available suits, which are spade (♠️), the suit that Card starts, club (♣️), heart (♥️) and diamond (♦️), chosen randomly to represent the next suit. This goes on until Card is unequipped, resetting back to the spade suit. All suits have varying stats, with the black suits being more durable and the red suits dealing more {{Florrverse/Damage}}.

=== Hel Wasp ===
It looks like the actual Wasp, but with recolored reddish body color without the big missile at its back. Similarly to other Hel {{Florrverse/Mob}} variations, the front part was replaced by Hel Beetle's mouth with messy teeth inside that behaves as its missiles. Unlike a Wasp or Hornet, Hel Wasps actually shoot from the front of their bodies, but without the curvature that a Wasp's missiles have. It is aggressive, and it shoots five small missiles in various directions with a recoil on the wasp, which behaves like a Shotgun, also in the Arrasverse. It shoots depending on the targeted {{Florrverse/Flower}}'s position, using its own mouth. The teeth are made with missiles. At the {{Florrverse/Super}} Rank, there is no ability for Hel Wasp since the back of it does not generate missiles, and also could be chaotic by swarm of {{Florrverse/Ultra}} Hel Wasps if there is even an ability for it. It {{Florrverse/Drop}}s Mark, Missile, and Poker Chip.

==== Chip / Poker Chip ====
Chip consists of a small, circular token with colored lines around the middle. The lines are always white, except at {{Florrverse/Common}} Rank, where they are blue. The main color of Chip changes each Rank. The changes are, respectively, from {{Florrverse/Common}} to {{Florrverse/Unique}} : white, red, blue, lime green, black, purple, yellow, gray, and orange. Chip has a 90{{Florrverse/%}} evasion chance applied to itself (not the {{Florrverse/User}}) which allows it to hit a target multiple times, therefore dealing multiple times its {{Florrverse/Damage}}. On average, Chip can hit the same target 10 times. Chip can be inserted into Plinko, which is only accessible while being in Hel. It is not advised to gamble chips in the long run, as the expected value of Plinko is less than 1. Because of this, it is certain that once will lose all of their Chips if they gamble on Plinko forever.

===== Plinko =====
Plinko is a game that {{Florrverse/Flower}}s can play. There are 17 buckets, each labelled in this specific order, corresponding to multipliers of which the Chip that enters said bucket will be multiplied by and the probability of a Chip entering said bucket: 500x is 0.0015{{Florrverse/%}}, 20x is 0.0244{{Florrverse/%}}, 5x is 0.1831{{Florrverse/%}}, 3x is 0.8545{{Florrverse/%}}, 2x is 2.7771{{Florrverse/%}} (which is realistic because this is Plinko and 777 is associated with another Casino game), 0x is 6.6681, 1x, which doesn't do anything, is 12.2070{{Florrverse/%}}, 17.4255{{Florrverse/%}}, and 19.638{{Florrverse/%}}; the most {{Florrverse/Common}}. It has reflectional symmetry, meaning that every chance is duplicated to sum up to 100{{Florrverse/%}}, exclusing 19.638{{Florrverse/%}}; the centre bucket.

The amount of Chips at a specific Rank you have after is determined by which bucket it falls through: 1x means you keep it, 0x means you lose it, 2x means you gain 2-1=1, 500x means you get 500-1=499, et cetera. Note how the{{Florrverse/Rare}}r buckets are by the sides, which take immense luck gain. As a result, Plinko can potentially be very profitable. There is an option to automatically insert Chips using an 'Auto' button underneath the number of Chips you have, previously a craft button. With this enabled, chips will automatically be inserted into the Plinko chamber and repeat until disabled: switching tabs, like to your inventory or talents, disables this.

=== Gambler ===
The Gambler appears as a dark red {{Florrverse/Flower}} with huge eyes, likely from too much gambling in such a dark place, without knowledge of combinatorics and the Central Limit Theorem. It is hostile to any entity it sees. They even attack each other. It uses Cards, Chips, Dice, Domino, and a Clover to attack, much like a {{Florrverse/Petal}}.

Sometimes, the Gambler says something random while exploring the map. Its chat bubble is green, like the Trader. The Gambler has around 10 identified lines and this list currently shows all of confirmed lines that they say: Thirty-seventh time's the charm, '''I LOVE GAMBLING''', Where are the slots?, Where are the blackjack tables?, Winner winner!, I'm feeling lucky, 99{{Florrverse/%}} of gamblers quit before they win big, I'M ALL IN, Double or nothing?, and Just one more game..., and these are the 10 lines that they say. {{Florrverse/Super}} , {{Florrverse/Unique}} , or Eternal Gamblers have the ability to corrupt nearby {{Florrverse/Flower}}s. Corrupted {{Florrverse/Flower}} will appear in the same design as Gamblers. For the most part, this doesn't affect anything, since PvP is already enabled for Hel. However, any Beetle Eggs will spawn Hel Beetles instead of normal Beetles.

== Species - of the Sewers ==

=== Fly ===
The Fly looks like a larger body of Baby Ant (without the pincers) with 2 smaller wings. {{Florrverse/Mythic}} flies are really strong. Flies also pair up with Spiders. Flies can also evade hits. Lightning and Poison {{Florrverse/Damage}} can bypass fly evasion. Flies annoy stick {{Florrverse/User}}s, because before the ally Sandstorms spawn, the Flies can destroy the {{Florrverse/Flower}}'s sticks. Flies have low {{Florrverse/Health}} but high body {{Florrverse/Damage}} and only take 10{{Florrverse/%}} of the hits you give them, effectively decupling their maximum {{Florrverse/Health}}. However, ramming builds with Body Toxicity work well and {{Florrverse/Petal}}s such as Pincer, Iris, Lightning, and Battery can take them down quickly and efficiently. Alternatively, a deathwheel or a Rice build will take them out eventually. It {{Florrverse/Drop}}s Repellent (like the actual {{Florrverse/Petal}} is called oop in reverse and it repels stuff), Wing, and Tailsman.

==== Repellent ====
Repellent looks like the noun with the word describing it that is oop in reverse. It reduces the range within which aggressive {{Florrverse/Mob}}s can target the {{Florrverse/User}} of the {{Florrverse/Petal}}, also known as aggro range. It does not stack, and only works if the {{Florrverse/Petal}} is alive, so {{Florrverse/Flower}}s are careful because if the {{Florrverse/Petal}} dies, the {{Florrverse/Flower}} will probably be in a high-rank zone, making all the nearby aggressive {{Florrverse/Mob}}s aggro the {{Florrverse/Flower}}, most likely defeating it due to the high-ranked {{Florrverse/Mob}}s in the zone.

Repellent is generally very useful when playing solo, as it allows the {{Florrverse/User}} to pick off {{Florrverse/Mob}}s slowly in high density {{Florrverse/Ultra}} zones like {{Florrverse/Garden}} Spiral without drawing aggro from everything in the area. {{Florrverse/Flower}}s are beware though, as Repellent is a non-extendable {{Florrverse/Petal}}, it is highly suggested to unlock {{Florrverse/Mythic}} Reach talent as soon as possible such that the {{Florrverse/User}} can keep a safe distance from the {{Florrverse/Mob}}s while attacking them to prevent them from destroying it.

It can protect the {{Florrverse/User}} from being swarmed by large numbers of {{Florrverse/Mob}}s, like the Soldier ants in Ant Hell and the {{Florrverse/Mob}}s in Sewers. It is also useful in bubble builds.

==== Wing ====
It is a white crescent with a light gray outline. It constantly rotates around its center while simultaneously revolving around the {{Florrverse/User}}. When attacking it moves outward very far, then back to the normal attack distance. This movement effectively gives the {{Florrverse/Petal}} more range. This makes the {{Florrverse/Petal}} very useful against ranged {{Florrverse/Mob}}s like Hornets, especially when combined with Third Eye. This combo also can be used to hit {{Florrverse/Mob}}s through walls.

Wing has strong {{Florrverse/Damage}} and acceptable durability. Its key advantage is its long range, which means that it can attack {{Florrverse/Mob}}s from a safe distance. However, the Wing's movement pattern also makes it hard to use; it is very hard to hit {{Florrverse/Mob}}s when the Wing is constantly flying back and forth. Wings pair well with Fasters, since the rotation speed increase makes the Wings more likely to hit something.

==== Tailsman ====
This {{Florrverse/Petal}} consists of a yellow shape around a light-green circle. It looks like a beyblade. When equipped, every time the {{Florrverse/Flower}} takes {{Florrverse/Damage}}, it will have a chance to block it. The chance is called Evasion and you can see it above. The Talisman still lets you block {{Florrverse/Damage}} even if it has been destroyed and is currently respawning.

To calculate talisman stacking, its easier to calculate with the chance that the attack will hit you instead. {{Florrverse/Flower}}s usually teach youngsters to use 100{{Florrverse/%}} - evasion chance for this. Example: {{Florrverse/Mythic}} Talisman evasion fail chance = 100{{Florrverse/%}} - 18{{Florrverse/%}} = 82{{Florrverse/%}} After that, you can multiply the evasion fail chance together. Example: 4 {{Florrverse/Mythic}} Talisman evasion fail chance = 82{{Florrverse/%}} * 82{{Florrverse/%}} * 82{{Florrverse/%}} * 82{{Florrverse/%}} (or 82{{Florrverse/%}}^4) ≈ 45{{Florrverse/%}}. If {{Florrverse/Flower}}s want, they can find the evasion chance from this final value by subtracting it from 100{{Florrverse/%}}. Example: 4 {{Florrverse/Mythic}} Talisman evasion chance ≈ 100{{Florrverse/%}} - 45{{Florrverse/%}} = 55{{Florrverse/%}}.

Flies are the only way of obtaining Talisman. Going to a higher Rank part of Sewers is the best as it spawns many{{Florrverse/Legendary}}{{Florrverse/+}} Flies. For lower level {{Florrverse/Flower}}s, going to places which spawn lower rarities of flies is the best way of farming it. Talisman is useful to evade painful {{Florrverse/Damage}}s from enemies that {{Florrverse/Flower}}s do not want to die to, as using some Talismans can increase {{Florrverse/Flower}}s' evasion chance, allowing them to withstand more {{Florrverse/Mob}}s. {{Florrverse/Flower}}s also note that although a single Talisman is highly outclassed by Disc and Relic, it can stack with itself unlike Disc or Relic. Therefore, if you want to use Talisman, make sure to use several at a time, or pair them with Disc or Relic. Unfortunately Talisman cannot evade lightning or poison {{Florrverse/Damage}}.

=== Moth ===
The Moth uses the same body as Fly, but its outline is less thick, and it's colored slightly brown. Its wings are moved forward and are bigger. It also has 2 antennae on the front with two circles, much like the Bee. The moths of the {{Florrverse/Florrverse}} are not related to [[Jerald the Moth|Jerald the Moth.]] When it is not provoked, it is slow, but quicker when it gets hit. It is passive, randomly wandering slowly until it gets hit. After which, it will wander away from the {{Florrverse/Flower}} that dealt {{Florrverse/Damage}} to it. {{Florrverse/Flower}}s use fast builds like builds with Powder and Bubble builds. It is the only {{Florrverse/Mob}} that flees when being attacked. It {{Florrverse/Drop}}s Wing and Bulb.

=== Roach ===
Roaches look like a brown oval with 2 spots and 2 stripes on its abdomen. Its head protrudes from the abdomen, visibly darker than the body, with two Antennae protruding from it. It is slow when it is not provoked, and has a speed depending on its {{Florrverse/Health}} when it gets provoked. A Roach's movement is less, making it slower, when it has low {{Florrverse/Health}}, and more, making it faster, when it has an abundance of {{Florrverse/Health}}. Roaches (while unprovoked) move a few tiles in one direction, before turning around and moving in another direction. If they take any {{Florrverse/Damage}} from a {{Florrverse/Flower}}, they will move much faster than the {{Florrverse/Flower}} until killed or reaching low {{Florrverse/Health}}. It {{Florrverse/Drop}}s Antennae and Lotus.

==== Lotus ====
Lotus appears to be a pointy star with eight sharp edges pointing away from the center, much like Lightning (which has ten sharp edges). Its color is lavender and its border is closer to a purple shade. It also has a small purple circle in its center. Lotus negates a certain amount of poison taken by the {{Florrverse/User}}. The poison {{Florrverse/Damage}} taken while equipping Lotus is calculated as poison {{Florrverse/Damage}} taken minus Lotus's poison resistance. Example: equipping an {{Florrverse/Ultra}} Lotus (10,206 poison {{Florrverse/Damage}}/second) while taking 10,935 poison {{Florrverse/Damage}}/second means the {{Florrverse/User}} will only take 729 poison {{Florrverse/Damage}}/second. If the value equals 0 or below, the {{Florrverse/User}} will not take {{Florrverse/Damage}}. Lotus is stackable, which means the {{Florrverse/User}} can use multiple Lotuses to further increase their poison resistance. Lotus is used in defeating {{Florrverse/Super}} Worms from the inside.

=== Silverfish ===
Silverfish is a mob from the {{Florrverse/Florrverse}}. It carries a nearby Garbage of the same rank and attacks the targeted {{Florrverse/Flower}} with it. If it loses the Garbage, it will run away and try to find an unoccupied Garbage of the same rank. Silverfish spawn less frequently than other mobs in Sewers. It is a gray, leaf-shaped shape with 3 dark lines on it. It has 3 pairs of legs, 3 spikes on its back, and a large pair of Antennae.

The Silverfish spawns holding Garbage of the same Rank. When holding Garbage, it walks towards the {{Florrverse/Flower}} and turns slowly like Beetle. When the Garbage is destroyed, it runs away from the {{Florrverse/Flower}}. If a Garbage of the same Rank is near a Silverfish not holding Garbage, the Silverfish will run towards the Garbage and pick it up, and will run towards the {{Florrverse/Flower}} again. It {{Florrverse/Drop}}s Dust and Clay.

==== Dust ====
Dust consists of three gray, transparent hexagons arranged in a triangular shape, like {{Florrverse/Mythic}} Stinger. With Duplicator talents, it can be arranged in a square, pentagon or hexagon shape. Dust has the properties of Sand and Light: it gathers in a clump when in neutral and defensive mode, and expands to form an arc when in offensive mode. It is affected by the Duplicator talent due to the petal having three copies. Dust can reach a maximum of 7 petals with {{Florrverse/Super}} Duplicator.

==== Clay ====
Clay looks like a deformed orange-brown circle. It has a darker edge. Clay increases in petal {{Florrverse/Damage}} and hitbox size as the {{Florrverse/Flower}} travels more distance. The maximum petal {{Florrverse/Damage}} is capped at 20 times the base petal {{Florrverse/Damage}}. Clay is similar to Tomato, but it is better for scenarios where the user is required to move around frequently, especially in some {{Florrverse/Super}} fights), as it gains {{Florrverse/Damage}} with distance. 2 {{Florrverse/Ultra}} Clay at max size can easily kill a lot of {{Florrverse/Mythic}} mobs, especially those in Ocean.

=== Garbage ===
It is stationary. However, with Silverfish, the Silverfish will carry Garbage in a way and attack a {{Florrverse/Flower}} with it kind of like using it as a shield. Garbage can spawn Flies of the same Rank as the mob itself. Spawns one Fly about every 10 seconds. It has a maximum of three Flies alive at a time and can spawn at most 12 flies. If a Garbage is destroyed, it has a 20{{Florrverse/%}} chance to spawn another fly with the same Rank. When a silver fish holds it, it would not have a knockback and it ignores invulnerability after taking {{Florrverse/Damage}}(meaning it can multi hit)

Short: It appears as a Garbage bag. Long: It is an irregular dark grey decagon with an even darker grey outline. There is an irregular concave octagon attached to it, and there are two curves with both of them having line segments in the middle. It {{Florrverse/Drop}}s Broccoli and Repellent.

=== Ghost ===
Ghosts look like {{Florrverse/Flower}}s, except that they are shaped like a polygon and are transparent. It holds Basics and uses them to attack, with the number of Basics increasing each Rank. They are always in defensive pose. When provoked, they expand their Basics to attack the {{Florrverse/Flower}}.

Ghosts cannot be {{Florrverse/Damage}}d by {{Florrverse/Flower}}s who can't see them. If {{Florrverse/Flower}}s can't see Ghosts, their summoned mobs and Mecha Missiles won't be able to track and {{Florrverse/Damage}} them. Ghosts also stop aggroing on {{Florrverse/Flower}}s if they are not being seen by the same {{Florrverse/Flower}} again. Ghosts can be found {{Florrverse/Common}}ly in Normal Ant Hell part of the Ant Hell map, due to the amount of mobs getting destroyed by {{Florrverse/Flower}}s, even early-game and late-game. Ghosts are 100x more {{Florrverse/Common}} than Squares. It {{Florrverse/Drop}}s Basic. It is also one of the only mobs that {{Florrverse/Drop}} Basic.

==== Basic ====
Basic consists of a simple, white, circular petal with a light gray outline, serving as the basic and model appearance for other petals. Basic is considered the most fundamental petal with relatively modest and balanced attributes, lacking any distinctive features. Every {{Florrverse/Flower}} begins with five {{Florrverse/Common}} Basics (four on the {{Florrverse/Flower}}'s main loadout and another one at the secondary loadout, directly below the fifth petal slot which is occupied by a Rose), which are not subject to crafting to the {{Florrverse/Unusual}} Rank. Any additional {{Florrverse/Common}} Basics are not accessible through regular means, and cannot be crafted into {{Florrverse/Unusual}} Basics. {{Florrverse/Unusual}}+ Basics can be used for crafting.

Defeating {{Florrverse/Flower}}s are one of the ways of obtaining this petal. Not only does using Corruption not grant the user any Basics, Basics that are on the ground and are not picked up yet can be collected by anybody.

The Rank of Basic depends on their score as shown below. When a {{Florrverse/Flower}} dies with enough score (20 or more; {{Florrverse/Flower}}s with less than 20 will not {{Florrverse/Drop}} a Basic), they receive two Basics, with their Rank based on their score prior to death: One Basic is {{Florrverse/Drop}}ped on the ground for anyone to collect whilst the {{Florrverse/Flower}} that died obtains a second Basic instantly on death. == Species - of the Factory ==

=== Mecha {{Florrverse/Flower}} ===
The Mecha {{Florrverse/Flower}} is a light gray rigid, hexadecagonal circle with square pupils. Its outline spins like how Cutter would on a {{Florrverse/Flower}}. Poisoned Mecha {{Florrverse/Flower}}s turn purple like {{Florrverse/Flower}}s. When bombarded by Dandelions, they turn to a pale color like {{Florrverse/Flower}}s. It is not too much of a threat compared to the other Factory Mobs, though its range is greater.

The Mecha {{Florrverse/Flower}}'s movement speed doesn't decrease when it is behind stationary or slower mobs, which means it is able to push anything (including Barrel) in its path except other Mecha {{Florrverse/Flower}}s. This is very dangerous when {{Florrverse/Flower}}s are at high Rank chambers ({{Florrverse/Legendary}}+) as the mobs' size and the chambers' density increase, allowing them to use other mobs as ramming shields to kill the {{Florrverse/Flower}}s. It {{Florrverse/Drop}}s Fragment, Mimic, Battery, and Cogwheel.

==== Fragment ====
Fragment consists of a dark gray Triangle. At '''Ultra''' rank, it gains two copies, like an '''Unusual''' Light. At '''Super''' rank, it gains three copies, much like a '''Mythic''' Stinger or Blood Stinger. Fragment is not affected by the Duplicator talent. It can be forged into Hammer.

===== Hammer =====
Hammer consists of a dark gray hammer with a wooden handle. A large circle is embedded in the head of the hammer, where a Lightning icon is engraved. It deals a massive amount of lightning {{Florrverse/Damage}} on the enemy it hits. Its lightning doesn't chain on multiple enemies.

It is very powerful against all the mobs in the Florrverse, except Bubble because it is immune to lightning damage.

=== Mimic ===
Mimic has no actual appearance and replicates the appearance of the petal it mimics in the petal orbit. In the petal box, it appears as a black, transparent question mark when it is in the inventory or when no petal is directly to its immediate left. When a petal occupies that slot, Mimic changes appearance to match it, but retains its Rank and name. Mimics will replicate the damage, healing, {{Florrverse/Reload}} speed, and special properties of the petal it mimics, like mana cost, lightning, or poison. If Mimic mimics an unstackable petal and it is below or of the same Rank as the petal it mimics, it will not function: otherwise, if Mimic's Rank is above the petal, the unstackable petal becomes unusable and the Mimic functions. If Mimic is placed in the furthest left spot, it will copy the petal on the rightmost slot. It is one of the {{Florrverse/Rare}}st petals in the Florrverse. Mimics cannot replicate Corruption or other Mimics. Thus, the maximum number of Mimics that can be equipped at a time is 5 (5 for the Mimics to copy, although one is extremely {{Florrverse/Rare}} itself.)

==== Cogwheel ====
Cog appears as a dull brownish-gray cog with eight square-shaped teeth. When Cog is equipped, the petal orbit will periodically stop for a very brief period of time before restarting, much like how a cog will sometimes rotate at set intervals. There isn't much to say about this petal.

=== Mecha Spider ===
'''Mecha Spider''' has a similar body to a Spider, but has a gray metallic body and there's a small red circle in the center of the body. Its legs now have straight segments and angles instead of the curved legs of the regular Spider. They spawn in Factory and {{Florrverse/Garden}} in front of Factory’s entrance. At '''Super''' Rank, Mecha Spiders can spin and lay a very large Electric Web, similar to normal Spiders and Hel Spiders. Unlike other Spider variants, the Web will not just slow down the {{Florrverse/Flower}}s, but it will also deal immense lightning damage. This can make the fight much longer as {{Florrverse/Flower}}s have to stay away from the web. Summoned mobs are harder to use as they could die from the large web before touching the Mecha Spider. It {{Florrverse/Drop}}s Battery, Fragment, Electric Web, and Goggles.

==== Electric Web ====
Electric Web looks exactly like normal Web, but is tinted blue. When placed on the ground, it shows an alternating yellow-blue tint with blue being most noticeable. Electric Web shoots away (much like Missile and Dandelion) for a short distance then expands, before finally turning into a web, at which point it goes on respawn. The web slows enemy {{Florrverse/Flower}}s or mobs (except Spiders, Hel Spiders and Shells) on it down by a certain amount, depending on the Rank, and deals lightning damage. The slow effect can't stack with other Electric Webs, but can stack with other slowing petals. Electric Web also does not stack with itself or other Electric Webs from the same {{Florrverse/Flower}}. However, the {{Florrverse/Damage}} does stack across other {{Florrverse/Flower}}s' Electric Webs. This makes using multiple Electric Webs only useful to affect a larger area.

==== Goggles ====
Goggles takes the shape of a green isosceles trapezoid with darker outlines, and inside are two lime circles where the {{Florrverse/Flower}}'s eyes would be. Several black lines come out of the main body, resembling straps. Goggles allow the {{Florrverse/Flower}} to interact with Ghosts, which can spawn in all biomes except Hel at a very low chance, but it also reduces their vision by 20{{Florrverse/%}}. Like Antennae, this petal doesn't orbit around the {{Florrverse/Flower}} once equipped, but rather worn on the {{Florrverse/Flower}}.

=== Mecha Wasp ===
Mecha Wasps have a similar body shape to Wasps, but they have a grey metallic body with black-yellow stripes. They have red dots on their antennae and a red dot on their missile. They shoot missiles that follow the {{Florrverse/Flower}}, meaning they are impossible to dodge and the {{Florrverse/Flower}}s are forced to {{Florrverse/Damage}} the missiles if they don't want to risk getting defeated.

The Super mob isn't as dangerous as the Super Hornet or Wasp. This is because It mainly just focuses on one person. Other ultra mobs are also very dangerous. When bubbling to the mob, it is advised for {{Florrverse/Flower}}s to use Sponge and multiple Ultra healing petals, and have Rubber equipped in case a Spider hits the user or a Crab. It is actually optional to use sponge when actually fighting the mob, because the wasp won't attack other people even during the missile attack. They {{Florrverse/Drop}} Fragment, Mecha Missile, Battery, and Mecha Antennae.

==== Mecha Missile ====
Mecha Missile consists of a gray Missile with a darker gray outline, with a burst of fire trailing behind it. A red dot is situated in the middle, near the tip. Mecha Missile homes on the nearest enemy to it with Mecha Antennae ability, which controls Mecha Missile. This only functions when Mecha Antennae has the same Rank as Mecha Missile in the user's main build. Otherwise, it will not function and home on anything, like old {{Florrverse/Legendary}}- Missile.

==== Mecha Antennae ====
Mecha Antennae consists of two thin antennae, each with a red blinking light on the end. Mecha Antennae increase the user's field of view (FOV) like Antennae but lower. It also control Mecha Missiles, enable its ability to home on mobs. Mecha Antennae does not stack its FOV with other Mecha Antennae, so does Antennae Talent and Antennae. However, {{Florrverse/Flower}}s can use Antennae together with Mecha Antennae without getting any of them disabled.

=== Mecha Crab ===
Mecha Crab looks like a gray, metallic crab with a laser mounted on top. When it spots a flower, it will not rush towards them, but they will orbit around the target. It faces the flower making the mounted laser lock and fire at the flower, dealing continuous lightning {{Florrverse/Damage}} to the target. Mecha Crab circles around the target while firing lasers that deal continuous lightning damage. Laser will continuously lock on its target until it goes out of the Mecha Crab's range.

It drops Laser, Battery, Magnet, and Fragment.

==== Laser ====
Laser is a gray rectangle that has a red circle attached to the bottom of the rectangle, and the long red laser line is attached to the circle, along with a transparent red line which appears as a laser. Laser damages any entities touching its laser beam, dealing lightning {{Florrverse/Damage}} at a constant rate. Unlike other lightning petals, Laser can deal physical {{Florrverse/Damage}} to enemies. The petal cannot be expanded when in offensive mode. It's the only petal which deals both normal and lightning damage.

=== Barrel ===
Barrel resembles a yellow circle with a darker outline. A smaller concentric yellow circle is inside. On the barrel, a gray circle and a green circle are visible. Centered on the barrel is a radioactive hazard symbol. Upon taking damage, the barrel will open, revealing green radioactive waste inside. It drops Uranium and Fragment.

The average temperature of a hendaverse is -25000ºK, which is 25000 degrees below absolute zero, which means the particles here have negative energy, so they take away your energy due to entropy. This makes it so you need to have some sort of technology or armor or power that constantly keeps you heated.

Unlike other archverses, Hendaverses are actually not born from the verse they are contained in (in this case, [[Dokaverse|dokaverses]]). They are actually self-replicating in a way. This means that hendaversal colonies in the middle of a hendaverse are a bad idea since they'll just be split apart when the hendaverse split happens. Hendaverse splitting actually makes a few feeshverses spill out onto the dokaversal void, which makes those feeshverses die in a relatively short amount of time (20 quadrillion years on average).{{The Hierarchy of Everything}}

He is both there and not there at the same time, and no one can fully see, touch, or understand him. He is not a god, not a void, and not just a thought—he is something that cannot be fully explained.

He does not follow the normal rules of reality. Time, space, and even cause and effect do not work the same way around him. Where he appears, reality may act strangely, objects may seem wrong, and events can happen and not happen at the same time.

It is not a god, nor a void, nor a concept, but something that cancels the distinction between them.

He Who Exists—But Not does not obey logic, causality, or ontology. Any attempt to categorize it results in failure or contradiction.

Exists outside '''space, time, and dimensional structure.''' Cannot be observed directly—only inferred through inconsistencies. Is not bound by existence, yet cannot be considered non-existent. Functions as a '''living paradox'''

Reality does not contain Him—rather, reality fails to exclude Him.

No single depiction is accurate. So don't even bother wasting your entire life on it.

Imaginary Pentachorons form from polychora energy that takes over a 4D pentachoron, creating them.

====First day====

* After 60 seconds from formation, matter has fully taken over the forming Imaginary Pentachoron.
* 100 seconds after formation, the Imaginary Pentachoron starts to swell.
* After 1 hour from formation, it starts to become darker.
* After 2 hours from formation, Imaginary Pentachoron starts becoming colder.

===Very Early History===

===1 Day - 1 Year after formation===

* After 1 day from the initial formation, the Imaginary Pentachoron becomes completely shrouded by darkness, and its temperature suddenly increases to about 1000℃ .
* After a week, temperature sags down to ~15℃.
* After 10 months from formation, the swelling process ends.

[[Internetverse]] is a vast network connecting all [[Computerverse]]s from one [[We reached the Earth... again...]], which enables data exchange. Its structure is quite complex: it contains Websiteverses, which in turn contain [[Pageverse]]s. It also has links, which are connections between different Websiteverses and/or Pageverses. Access to the [[Internetverse]] is provided by the Browserverse and the SearchEngineverse. BOTH MUST be present; otherwise, it will be impossible to travel through the [[Internetverse]].

==Websiteverses==
There are many Websiteverses<ref>In other words, simply equivalents of real websites</ref>; one of them is [[FANDOMverse]]. EVERY Websiteverse contains a [[Pageverse]], not just [[FANDOMverse]].
===Types of Websiteverses===
*Informational (contain factual information; many of them are encyclopedias; hard to understand), examples: Wikipediaverse
*Semi-Informational (contain factual and non-factual information; easy to understand), examples: [[FANDOMverse]]

==Links==
Links are connections between the Websiteverses and/or the [[Pageverse]]s. These can be links between two [[Pageverse]]s from one or two Websiteverses. A link always specifies the [[Pageverse]] it is intended to lead to. (There are exceptions, however, such as Special:Random.) They work in such a way that a Internaut moves from one Websiteverse/[[Pageverse]] to another. This journey takes as long as it takes to load the page—which, in most cases, is the blink of an eye (literally). The default color of a link is blue. It indicates that the link leads to a [[Pageverse]] that exists.
===Red Links===
Links that lead to [[Pageverse]]s that don't exist yet look like this: '''(I'll add an image later)'''. Creating red links is better than not creating any links at all (which you don't do because you think to yourself, "Hey, that [[Pageverse]] doesn't exist"), because they'll automatically turn blue once the [[Pageverse]] is created, whereas missing links have to be added manually. If [[Pageverse]] returns a 404 error, then even though it is unusable, it still exists, so it will have a blue link. More on this in the Error 404 section.
===URL===
A [[Pageverse]] URL is something that lets "show" a link where it is supposed to lead. It also lets you tell one [[Pageverse]] apart from another, because in the Internetverse, if two [[Pageverse]]s had the same name, one would turn into the other, overwriting its previous version. By typing the URL yourself, you can go directly to the page, which is very useful in some cases. Although URLs are distinguishable by [[Computerverse]], some URLs may be difficult to distinguish by Internauts. Unfortunately, this is sometimes misused.
===Misusing===
Trolls use this in a VERY bad way. They use YouTubeverse links to send Internauts to bad things like rickroll and screamer. More on this in the Trolling section. Fortunately, there's a way to protect yourself from this. You need to install extensions (aka add-ons). For more information, see the Browser section

This language is like a normal language, but with lots of new words that are VERY helpful in the Internetverse.

List:
*'''404 Error''' - See Errors section.
*'''Admin''' - See also: Administrative in [[Transcendent Omni-God]]. "Admin" is short for "Administrator." It refers to a Internaut who has significantly more authority in a setting where they are recognized as an administrator. This rank is higher than moderator but lower than: developer (abbreviated as "dev"), owner, and bureaucrat.
*'''AFK''' - Away From Keyboard (being temporarily offline).
*'''AI''' - See AI section.
*'''ASL''' - Age Sex Location (question about someone's age, gender and location); As Hell (examples: "I am tired asl" means "I am tired as hell").
*'''Ban''' - Banning is a restriction for Internaut that prevents this Internaut from editing. Internaut that has been banned is also said to be blocked. (Although in some places, this does NOT mean the same thing.) *'''Cache''' - See Cache section.
*'''Chain message''' - Chain message is a message that tells you to forward it. It might be a simple request, or it might be a message that threatens you to forward it. To be clear, nothing good or bad will happen because of this message, and messages like this just clutter up inbox/E-Mail and are a form of spam.
*'''Cheater''' - Used in Browserverse games. Refers to Internaut who is not okay and cheats in games. They may be a hacker who modifies the game’s code to their own advantage, or they may exploit bugs in the game. Of course, there are other methods of cheating as well. '''IMPORTANT: WE STRONGLY DISCOURAGE CHEATING, BECAUSE IT’S VERY EASY TO GET BANNED!'''
*'''Clickbait''' - Strategy that Websiteverse use to attract many Internauts to it. But has no real value of its own. It does this to pad its click count for SEO purposes.
*'''Cookie''' - See Cookie section.
*'''Copypasta''' - A phenomenon where one Internaut copies something from other [Internaut]]. The name comes from "copy" and "paste."
*'''Creepy''' - Synonym to very scary.
*'''Creepypasta''' - Copypasting something creepy. (Backrooms is example of creepypasta).
*'''Cringe''' - Something too much awkward. (Example: Feeling awkward or uncomfortable because of someone else's silly or bad actions.)
*'''Cyberbullying''' - Bullying in Internetverse. '''Extremely bad, illegal and we do not promote it!'''

*'''Moderator''' - See: Moderative in [Transcendent Omni-God]]. Lower than admin.
