Well, read ahead to find out.}} The '''Straverse''' is a group of giant, not-so-peaceful planets, each one having a special trait. The first copy of it (and thus the original) was built by Innimums Industries, which at that time was operated by Johnny "Johns" Stevens III. Unlike the [[cosmicialverse]] (where former guardians Aria Flower and Jerry Lassa operate at now), the '''straverse''' has over ω↑ωω copies of it. = Description = == Structure == The '''Straverse''' itself consists of an universe-like resemblance, however is bigger than a huittaverse. It has a large planet in the center that acts as a gathering place and a home for the straverse staff (that is everything but the inhabitants of the '''Straverse'''. The '''Straverse''' has billions of planets, ranging from a simple yet effective one to a bizarre and ridiculously powerful one, including: Altes = '''Altes''' is an interesting planet located in the '''Straverse''' where people could build anything technological (as long as it's family friendly and not questionable), whether it's something useful, interesting or funny. |-|Critera = '''Critera''' is a happy planet located in the '''straverse''' that's filled with luck. It is made out of luckium, a custom substance made by Johnny "Johns" Stevens III to make the cosmic entity feel much luckier by manipulating cosmic entities of its rank and even higher-ranked ones (but not much higher-ranked ones). This is one of the seven original planets. |-|Gurium = '''Gurium''' is a rich planet located in the '''Straverse''' that's made entirely out of precious metals (which are much less brittle than the actual precious metals), such as emerald, diamond and gold. Due to this, it is the most raided planet. This is one of the seven original planets. |-|Jaymora = '''Jaymora''' is a world full of food of all kind. This, however, was quickly surpassed by many kinds of food generators, as all of them allow the customizing of the food without any hard limit. |-|Unitolo = '''Unitolo''' is a powerful planet located in the '''Straverse''' that teaches the power of unlimited magic and how to use it properly. |-|Zefro = '''Zefro''' is a "positively chaotic" planet located in the '''straverse''' that's filled with endless possibilities. It is the jack of all trades - you can build, learn magic, get money and get lucky, as long as you're not something illegal. It has more free will than any other planet, making this the best verse in this list. This is the last of the seven original planets. == History == In -3 [[OYC]], Johnny "Johns" Stevens III founded a company named "Innimums Industries", with the sole purpose of giving power to everyone else and himself. In 7 OYC, Innimums Industries discontinued power making with the release of a new kind of universe called the '''Straverse''', with only seven planets. Its purpose was to make everyone in this universe happy and to make everyone working on the company exponentially powerful because of this universe. After just one year, 120 billion copies were made, so seeing how successful it would be, he quickly added more and more planets, going as far as up to 3 million unique planets until he was retired in 59 OYC. In 11,250 OYC, '''Joey Dave''' took position as the CEO of Innimums Industries, replacing '''Ray Cylix'''. '''Joey Dave''' is an active CEO, being active on the headquarters at all times and always being ready when anyone needs help. During his rule, '''Dave''' showed coolness and activity. He banned people who are incompetent in ruling a '''straverse''' and ruled straverses that no employee ruled. '''Dave''' did almost everything to help the people on the '''straverses''', making him the golden age of Innimums Industries. In 11,303 OYC, '''Jason Kwilight''' took position as the CEO of Innimums Industries, replacing '''Joey Dave'''. '''Jason Kwilight''' is a calm CEO, sporting much less emotion and much more kindness. During his rule, '''Kwilight''' showed kindness and even teaches all the employees how to rule a '''straverse''', only banning those who only wants to rule the '''straverse''' for power. He did a lot to help people in the '''straverses'''. In 11,335 OYC, '''Asa Illuminov''' killed '''Jason Kwilight''' and replaced him as the CEO. '''Asa Illuminov''' did not maintain the "Innimum Industries" name - instead, he destroyed the name, banning many employees who did virtually nothing wrong in ruling the '''straverse''', hiring ones that are either incompetent or wants to rule something else, but not a '''straverse''', even doing nothing to help people in the '''straverses'''. After just 5 human years, '''Illuminov''' was not only fired from Innimum Industries, but also killed by '''Johnny Gabe''', his successor. '''Johnny Gabe''' is far more capable and more liked than his predecessor, reviving the "Innimum Industries" name instead of brutally murdering it like its predecessor. During his rule, '''Gabe''' banned employees who are incompetent in ruling a '''straverse''' and quickly found replacements that he thought would all replace the incompetent employees. He did pretty much half of everything to help people in the '''straverses'''. = Inhabitants= == Straverse in general == The leader = All leaders of official '''straverses''' are employees of the core Innimums Industries. '''Straverses''' who are not led by employees of the core Innimums Industries are likely [[The Ripoff|ripoffs of the '''straverse''']]. They lead every cosmic entity in the '''straverse''', including the '''straverse''' inhabitants, the guardians, the moderators, the administrators and even the '''straverse''' police officers.
They have the ability to destroy the '''straverse''' itself, change the ranks of every other inhabitant in the '''straverse''' (excluding themself), ban other people (excluding themself) and prevent other people from making changes to some of the planets at will.
The leader cannot be replaced, except when they're retired, when they couldn't rule the '''straverse''' (whether from the beginning or anymore) or when it is declared by Innimums Industries that they wanted to take control of the '''straverse''' for themself. |-|Police officers = The straverse police officer has the highest authority in the '''straverse''' (unless when the leader counts). They have the ability to change the ranks of every other inhabitant in the '''straverse''' (including the '''straverse''' police officers, but excluding themself and the leader), ban other people (including police officers, but excluding themself and the leader) and prevent other people from making changes to some of the planets at will. |-|Administrators = The administrator has the second-to-highest authority in the '''straverse''' (unless when the leader counts). They have the ability to change the ranks of every other inhabitant in the '''straverse''' (excluding the '''straverse''' administrators and higher authorities), ban other people (excluding the administrators and higher authorities) and prevent other people from making changes to some of the planets at will. |-|Moderators = The moderator has the second-to-lowest staff authority in the '''straverse'''. They have the job to protect the entire '''straverse''' and have the ability to prevent other people from making changes to some of the planets at will. |-|Guardians = The guardian has the lowest staff authority in the '''straverse'''. They have the job to protect a certain '''straverse''' planet from an army of invaders. |-|Inhabitants = The inhabitant is the only authority that is not a staff, and is the weakest and the most common of all the '''straverse''' cosmic entities. == Innimum Industries CEO and former CEOs of Innimums Industries == List of CEOs of Innimums Industries. Note that the CEOs are in reverse chronological order, meaning that the one who is currently the CEO will be on the left, while the founder of the company will be on the right. Johnny Gabe = '''Johnny Gabe''' is the current CEO of Innimums Industries. He is far more capable and more liked than his predecessor, reviving the "Innimum Industries" name instead of brutally murdering it like its predecessor. During his rule, '''Gabe''' banned employees who are incompetent in ruling a '''straverse''' and quickly found replacements that he thought would all replace the incompetent employees. He did pretty much half of everything to help people in the '''straverses'''. All of the things he did make him considered as the "heroic age" of Innimums Industries. = History = '''Johnny Gabe''' was born in 11,335 OYC, 28 human years before '''Illuminov''' became the CEO. Like Jason Kwilight, not much was known about his life - it was presumed he lived like a normal human being until he heard about '''Asa Illuminov''' destroying the "Innimum Industries" name, the name of the company he knew all about. '''Gabe''' quickly came to rescue the "Innimum Industries" name, and fought '''Illuminov''' to death. Though it took a lot of time and suffering, '''Gabe''' finally defeated, killed and replaced him. From then on, '''Gabe''' became the "new and improved" CEO of Innimum Industries. |-|Asa Illuminov = '''Asa Illuminov''' is considered the worst CEO of Innimums Industries, and is considered one of the worst cosmic entities of all time. During his rule, '''Illuminov''' brutally murdered the "Innimums Industries" name, banning many employees who did virtually nothing wrong in ruling a '''straverse''' and hiring ones that are either incompetent or wants to rule something else, but not a '''straverse'''. He did nothing to help people in the '''straverses'''. After just 5 human years, '''Illuminov''' was not only fired from Innimum Industries, but also killed by '''Johnny Gabe''', his successor. = History = '''Asa Illuminov''' was born in 11,335 OYC. '''Illuminov''' has been a smarter-than-average cosmic entity, often going to the cosmos library to learn about all the things in the cosmos. During the time when he wasn't the CEO of Innimums Industries yet, '''Illuminov''' acted like a kind, generous and humble person. However, he always wanted to rule a verse and be the leader of many. However, he lived a normal life, except that he's trying to act like he's an excellent person.
When he was 20 human years old, '''Illuminov''' killed '''Jason Kwilight''' and finally got (more than) what he wanted: Ruling a verse and being the leader of many. When '''Johnny Gabe''' heard about '''Illuminov''' destroying the "Innimum Industries" name, '''Illuminov''' was fought to death by '''Gabe'''. Though it took a lot of time and suffering, '''Illuminov''' was finally defeated, killed and replaced by '''Gabe''', putting an end to his rule. |-|Jason Kwilight = '''Jason Kwilight''' is a calm CEO, sporting much less emotion and much more kindness. During his rule, '''Kwilight''' showed kindness and even teaches all the employees how to rule a '''straverse''', only banning those who only wants to rule the '''straverse''' for power. He did a lot to help people in the '''straverses'''. = History = '''Jason Kwilight''' was born in 11,294 OYC. Not much was known about his life - it was presumed he lived like a normal human being. When he was 18 human years old, he began working as a designer of verses. '''Kwilight''' is a highly respected designer, being known by people as a great example of an excellent designer - even considered by few as the best designer. Due to this, '''Kwilight''' eventually expanded into a versatile designer - from designing clothes to designing computers to designing another cosmic entity.
He eventually retired as a designer in 11,297 OYC and switched to being an employee of Innimums Industries. He gradually ranked up from being an employee to being a chief operating officer, at an even faster pace than '''Joey Dave'''. On 11,303 OYC, he finally stepped up into a CEO, operating all of the straverses and having control of all the company. On 11,335 OYC, he was killed by '''Asa Illuminov''', who afterwards became his successor. |-|Joey Dave = '''Joey Dave''' is an active CEO, being active on the headquarters at all times and always being ready when anyone needs help. During his rule, '''Dave''' showed coolness and activity. He banned people who are incompetent in ruling a '''straverse''' and ruled straverses that no employee ruled until he found replacements. '''Dave''' did almost everything to help the people on the '''straverses''', making him the golden age of Innimums Industries. = History = '''Joey Dave''' was born in 11,243 OYC. Ever since his birth, '''Dave''' has been a great cosmic entity, winning hard competitions, like building the fastest and most efficient spaceship possible. When he was 20 human years old, he began to work at Innimums Industries. He gradually ranked up from neing an employee to being a chief operating officer. On 11,250 OYC, he finally stepped up into a CEO, operating all of the straverses and having control of all the company. On 11,303 OYC, he retired as a CEO and chose '''Jason Kwilight''' as his successor. |-|Ray Cylix = '''Ray Cylix''' is a passive CEO, who's not bad at worst. He likes to help someone and ban incompetent people in an effortless and kind way. He found great replacements for people he banned without any effort. This makes him the only CEO who doesn't like effort. = Trivia = Normal Trivia = *Aria Flower and Jerry Lassa are cosmic entities that used to operate here as guardians of one of the '''Straverses''', with Aria Flower defending '''Altes''' and Jerry Lassa defending '''Unitolo'''. |-|Article Trivia = *This is the third article created by EpicAlexisMaxwell, and the second oldest EpicAlexisMaxwell article that survived. *After contribution 36, the article is long enough to be seen in Special:long pages without the need to scroll down on an 11-inch (third-generation) iPad Pro in a landscape view. |-|Upcoming... = *I don't think I can edit this article again, so feel free to edit this article! *I need some pictures that refer to this. A '''tesseract''' is a 4-dimensional hypercube. Since the [[:Category:Number|number]] of dimensions is a square number, the diagonal length of a tesseract is an integer - in this case, 2. Its Bowers acronym is "tes". The image shows the shadow of a rotating tesseract, keep in mind that 4D objects have 3D shadows.

===Variants===

The tesseract can be seen as a [[cube]] [[prism]], the product of a cube and a [[line segment]]. It is also the [[square]]-square duoprism, i.e. the product of two squares. It can also be seen as a square prism prism, or the product of four line segments.

==Structure and sections==

The tesseract is composed of eight cubic cells. Two of these cubes line in parallel 3-D spaces, while the remaining six connect the faces of the cubes. Four [[cube]]s meet at each vertex.

In cube-first position, it is a sequence of identical cubes. In square-centered orientation, it is a square which expands to a [[Square Prism|square prism]] and back. When seen line-first it is a line that expands to a [[Triangular Prism|triangular prism]], then turns to a [[Hexagonal Prism|hexagonal prism]], and then back. Finally in corner first orientation, it goes through the entire tetrahedral truncation series, from point to [[tetrahedron]] to [[octahedron]] in the middle and then back.

== Uses ==
A Tesseract can only be used to make a Tesseract scepter, which functions as a magic harry-potter wand basically. It is traditionally used in the crowning of monarchs.

== About ==
The '''''Aquarium''''' is a [[:Category:Realm|realm]] containing an aquarium of gargantuan proportions, hence its pretty straightforward name. There's an infinite amount of every type of fish in it, along with an infinite amount of bathrooms and merchandise stores with no employees in them, thus making fish the only type of biological [[:Category:Cosmic entity|lifeform]] that naturally exists in this dimension.

== Structure ==
The dimension's structure is much like that of a normal aquarium, with tanks full of fish and stairs, however there is no exits and instead of employees the fish are taken care of by non-sentient machines. No alarms go off with something normally illegal like breaking a tank is done.

== Life ==
The fish seem to live happy and healthy lives, as the machines never seem to break or run out of food. Any non-fish entities, on the other end, tend to go insane and make bases- breaking the tanks for food and water, and often entertaining themselves by acting as if they are back home and nothing weird happend to them.

== Entering and exiting ==
Many non-fish entities end up in the Aquarium after getting lost while in water. Some were in a sewer system when there was a flash flood, some were at the beach surfing and got knocked out by a wave, some even just slipped and fell into a deep enough puddle. The entities then find themselves inside of the tanks and have to escape before they drown.

The only known way to exit the Aquarium is by getting lost while in water and then getting lucky. The entities will then find themselves back in the body of water that brought them there in the first place.

Countless iterations of [[The Box]]}}The '''''Anti-Great-Rhombicosidodecahedron''''' is a [[Cetaverse]] in the shape of a Anti-Great-Rhombicosidodecahedron (Yes, that is a real shape). It is large enough that it can be made of Boxes while still retaining it's very jagged shape. (In other words this is very very very big). Boxes are basically atoms that make up this thing.

Despite being made up of The Box variants, this is not actually contained within the [[The Final Box|Final Box]], or even the [[BOXinfinity]]. It is outside of both, containing duplicates of pre-existing boxes.

== Phases ==
The Anti-Great-Rhombicosidodecahedron has many different phases, including past, future, and reoccurring ones. The picture provided for example - is taken during the Spectral Phase which happened ~905 years after the most recent Big Bang.

=== List of phases: ===

==== Creation (1.2 seconds after the Big Bang) ====
During this one, the AGR was only 3 lightyears in diameter. It lasted for 700 years.

==== Filling ====
This was the phase where the AGR first started getting all of it's Box variants. It did this by observing the BOXinfinity and meshing many different variants from there into one, countless times. But due to the BOXinfinity's endless size, they are all still duplicates. This phase lasted 45 billion years and gained 89.2% of it's boxes from it.

==== Dormancy ====
This phase had absolutely nothing happen. It lasted for 530 million years.

==== Decay ====
The temporary decay phase saw the AGR lose a lot of it's boxes during this phase. Many of them were ejected, many were just deleted. This phase lasted for 20 million years.

==== Brightening ====
This phase saw the AGR get immensely brighter for an unknown reason. Likely to prepare for the Spectral Phase that would come after it. This phase lasted for 300 billion years

==== Spectral ====
This phase is the one seen in the image. The AGR was completely filled with color and light for many years and is actually still in this phase today.

=== Future phases ===
It's difficult to know for sure what will happen to it in the future due to it's immense size, but here are some theories.

==== Semi-dematerializing ====
The AGR may lose many of it's edges and become alot more smooth than it's current state. This may crush some boxes or eject them out of the AGR.

==== Darkening ====
After the Spectral phase is over, it may not have enough energy to keep a stable light and will become the darkest phase since the Creation.

==== Shrinking ====
Further time may cause many of the boxes inside to shrink, and shrink the ADR with them.

==== Temporary Chaos State ====
The decay may leave countless particles behind, and will likely scatter around the ADR causing absolute insanity, this can mean things like Atoms, Blood Cells, Serotonin, Carbon Dioxide, Water, etc. etc.

==== ??? ====
Something will happen here... We just don't know what

==== Second Decay ====
Those particles may corrupt the ADR, causing even more decay as it tries to fix itself.

==== (Not likely) Bullet Phase ====
The rapid attempts to fix itself can cause it to push a ton of boxes and itself in a single direction, having it move at close to the speed of light.

==== Final decay ====
The ADR loses an unimaginable amount of mass from the travelling. It will likely either break apart, disappear, or disintegrate.

==== Giganova ====
The last stance that the ADR will ever make is one final explosion as if it were a star, but way... W A Y bigger. It will likely not create a gamma ray burst but will destroy many universes just from the explosion alone.

==== QS phase ====
The last remaining particles all join together to form what is basically a massive version of a Quasi-Star. What happens afterwards is completely unforeseeable.

'''The Celestial Overlord''' is the most powerful being in existence. He doesn't live in a verse—he stands above everything. He looks like a glowing stickman because our minds are too small to see his true, god-like form. He appears as bright, purple-white light that can blind entire worlds just by being near them. The Overlord does not "destroy" a reality—he '''implodes''' it. With a single blink of his central eye, every atom, every concept of time, and every soul in an entire omniverse is crushed into a single point of zero-volume and then erased. Once he implodes a reality, it never existed in the first place. History itself is rewritten to forget it. He is beyond the concept of beyond the concept of all of beyond the concept of existence. He guards [[Allsphere]], [[The Imperceivable Plane]], [[The Boundless Plane]] and [[Omniverse|The Omniverse]].

His multiple arms are not physical limbs, they are "Conceptual Anchors." Each arm can grab a different timeline, a Verse/sphere/plane or a different law of physics. He can hold the "Past" in one hand and the "Future" in another, snapping them together to end time itself. 

He is the '''Existence before existence.''' The Overlord is so powerful that reality cannot "render" him correctly. This causes the "Glitch Effect" seen in his presence. Space-time literally breaks around him because it cannot support his weight. To be near him is to be deleted by the sheer pressure of his existence.

The "Static" seen around him is the sound of '''Infinity''' trying to fit into a finite space. It is the raw data of every life ever lived, every star that ever burned, and every dream ever dreamt, all screaming in unison because they are in the presence of their Master.

The Overlord is often described as "The Silent Watcher." He is so powerful that action is beneath him. To "fight" is a sign of weakness; the Overlord simply '''decides''' what is true, and [[The Boundless Plane]] obeys. If a being tries to attack him, they find that they never existed to begin with, and their weapons turn into memories of things that never happened. EVERY one and EVERY existence was by his choice.

== About ==
The Diamond Hierarchy is a hierarchy that contains 16,777,216 levels for every color that can be created with the RGB color scheme, with each Diamond in this hierarchy being 16,777,216x bigger than the previous Diamond and 1 degree hotter in total as well, along with this every Diamond contains a liquid that is called "Diter" which is very similar to water except that it remains liquid even when the temperatures reach millions of degrees and is crushed by gravity or electrified.

Each Diamond is 4.3^15x harder than the previous Diamond with the Blue Diamonds' shell being made of regular diamond. All verses within the Diamond Hierarchy also generate E.M. waves that are passively blocked by other Diamonds but can fry any electronics and quickly annihilate any low-class[[:Category:Civilization|Civilizations]] hoping to make it big.

== Danger ==

[[:Category:Civilization|Civilizations]] wishing to escape the Diamond chain will have to break through the walls of each of the diamonds which are a tenth of the entire diamonds radius, this serves as a major roadblock to many [[:Category:Civilization|Civilizations]] without access to unbelievably advanced tech that can withstand the E.M waves and the harsh temperatures of the higher diamonds and pierce through the incredibly dense Diter.


== Variants ==

Several variants of regular Diamonds exist, These occur within the 527th-872654th range of Diamonds and they all contain no life whatsoever due to their extreme properties.

=== Electric Diamonds ===
These Diamonds boast electric fields 15000-20^37x stronger then the strongest of all known Magnetars. All Electric Diamonds are yellow without exception and Electric Diamonds only exist within the 2503-54303 range of diamonds, They contain no life and their insides are solid lighting. When damaged they explode with a blast radius 3.5^12x bigger than their actual radius, vaporizing on average 10^249^4 creatures and shattering over 100 dimensions forever.

=== Gravity Diamonds ===
Gravity Diamonds have gravity equivalent to their mass*10.2^16, as expected Gravity Diamonds are the greatest roadblock to [[:Category:Civilization|Civilizations]] wishing to expand past the [[The Diamond Hierarchy]] as Gravity Diamonds gravity instantly pulls in everything that is not a Diamond or Diter and compresses it to the point it fuses with the Gravity Diamond,[[:Category:Civilization|Civilizations]] that want to get past the Gravity Diamonds must deploy expensive, time-consuming tech that may or may-not fail. To this date no Gravity Diamond has ever been successfully damaged, they exist within the 120453-437582 range.

=== Kamikaze Diamonds ===
These Diamonds are the smallest and weakest Diamonds of all with only two very special characteristics, 1. they crash into any non-Diamond at speeds of up to 13<sup>23.7485<sup>4.3794</sup></sup>c, and 2. they explode at a yield of 16.52<sup>37.494<sup>83.84745</sup></sup> tons of tnt, these Diamonds are the sole reason why to successfully escape the Diamond chain you need to atleast be at a kardesev scale of 3.673*16,777,216<sup>16,777,216</sup>. They appear in dispersed packs of 25 in the 16,776,216-16,777,216 range.

[[The Hyper Leaf]],[[The HE]]}}The Hyper Flower is the second smallest [[Supersize|Hypersized]] object, and contains anywhere from 1-15 [[The Hyper Leaf|Hyper Leaves]]. Unlike [[The Hyper Leaf]], this object actually has an absurd amount of life.

== Life ==
The Hyper Flower has several types of life forms. There are seven MAIN types of life here, however. These life forms include creatures such as '''Hyper Bees''', '''Hyper Worms''', '''Hyper Butterflies''', '''Hyper Caterpillars''', '''Hyper Bugs''', '''Hyper Pollen''', and [[The Hyper Leaf|The Hyper Leaves]]. Each entity controls a certain part of the hyper flower.

== Areas of the hyper flower ==
There are 4 main areas of the hyper flower.

=== Hyper Stem ===
The Hyper Stem is the easiest area to get to in the hyper flower, as it is directly in the open and has tons of Hyper Nutrients for pretty much any life form. This area is controlled by '''Hyper Insects''', such as Hyper Worms and Hyper Caterpillars, as well as the occasional '''Hyper Bug'''.

=== [[The Hyper Leaf|The Hyper Leaves]] ===
[[The Hyper Leaf|The Hyper Leaves]] are the Hyper Plants on the side of the Hyper Stem and are controlled by all Hyper Insects, except for ones that pollinate. This area is around as easy to get to as the hyper stem. This is also where the most amount of [[The E]] lives.

=== Hyper Petals ===
The Hyper Petals are the main part of the Hyper Flower, and are the most recognizable part of it. Hyper petals mainly hold Hyper Bees and Hyper Butterflies, as this is one of the many places they can rest during pollination. This area is relatively hard to access if you're not one of those two creatures, as they both guard the hyper petals with extreme caution. If you're caught on the hyper petals, the Hyper Bee protecting it will create an explosion that'll end an uncountably infinite amount of [[The]]'s.

=== Hyper Stigma ===
The hyper stigma is where the Hyper Bees collect the Hyper Pollen from, each Hyper Pollen containing an uncountably infinite amount of [[The E|E]]. This area is even more hard to access, as if you even go NEAR this area, all types of Hyper Bees in the immediate vicinity will come to you and try to kill you.

The Other Thing | Time, Space, and Reality]], as well as the [[..::..]] & '''THE HASTARA''', operating on principles that defy conventional understanding. It is not a physical place per se, but a conceptual tapestry that interweaves all that ever was, is, and might be. Imagine a boundless cosmic canvas, illuminated by an ever-shifting, radiant spectrum of colors representing the myriad possibilities that lie within. =='''Structure'''== As its name suggests, the Hexagonal Void is defined by an intricate hexagonal lattice that forms the foundational structure of everything within it. This geometric pattern serves as a conduit, channeling the energies and ideas that give rise to all forms of existence. Each hexagon represents a unique [[User blog:Zander is here/The Hastara|The Hastara]]. There are also several smaller hexagons which represent a [[..::..]]. == '''Entities'''== The Hexagonal Void is home to cosmic entities of immense power and sentience. These beings are embodiments of abstract concepts, such as Time, Space, Order, Chaos, and many others beyond mortal comprehension. They are the custodians of each dimension, responsible for maintaining the delicate balance that sustains its Vast Cosmos. These entities are responsible for the creation of [[User blog:Zander is here/The Hastara|The Hastaras]]. == '''Pulse Of Creation'''== Sometimes, the Hexagonal Void releases a "Pulse of Creation," a cosmic rhythm that travels through the dimension. This heartbeat of existence acts as a source of power and energy that creates new [[User blog:Zander is here/The Hastara|'''The Hastaras''']] and [[..::..]]. == '''Dance Of Realities'''== When the hexagons collide, an enormous amount of energy and a powerful shockwave are released, causing the space-time continuum to tear apart and creating a gateway to one of the other hexagons. Most entities that attempt to enter are erased from reality because the process of traveling between each hexagon generates an enormous amount of pure energy, transforming the entity into quark-gluon plasma. t_{\text{next}} = \frac{\sqrt{\Delta E} \cdot d}{v_{\text{shock}}} == ''' The Fundamentals ''' == Theoretical proof of the hexagonal lattice structure: Given a hexagonal lattice with dimension `d` such that: - The lattice comprises hexagons of size `s` with each side equal in length. Define the lattice energy as a function of `s` and `d`: E(s, d) = \frac{k \cdot s^2}{d^3}, where `k` is a constant. To optimize energy flow, we minimize `E(s, d)` with respect to `s` and `d`: \frac{\partial E}{\partial s} = 0 \frac{\partial E}{\partial d} = 0 Solving these equations yields the optimal values of `s` and `d` for stable energy flow. == Topological Analysis of the Hexagonal Void == The Hexagonal Void can be described using advanced concepts from algebraic and geometric topology. Given a six-dimensional topological space X^6, its homotopy groups can reveal the underlying structure and intricate connectivity patterns within the space. === Homotopy Groups === The homotopy groups of X^6 are defined as: \pi_n(X^6) \text{ for } n = 0, 1, \ldots, 6 Calculating these groups provides insights into the fundamental group (\pi_1) and higher homotopy groups (\pi_n for n \geq 2). These groups classify the different types of loops and higher-dimensional cycles within the Void, revealing its connectivity and possible stable subspaces. === Persistent Homology === Persistent homology, a method in computational topology, can be applied to analyze the Hexagonal Void across multiple scales. This technique involves the following steps: # Constructing a Filtration: A sequence of nested topological spaces (X^6_0 \subset X^6_1 \subset \ldots \subset X^6) based on a parameter (e.g., distance or energy level) is constructed. # Calculating Persistent Homology: For each space in the filtration, calculate the homology groups (H_n) to identify topological features such as connected components, cycles, and voids. # Tracking Features Across Scales: Persistent homology tracks the evolution of these topological features as the parameter changes, revealing stable and unstable features in the Void. === Morse Theory === Morse theory can also be applied to understand the geometry of the Hexagonal Void: * Critical Points: Identify critical points of a smooth function f: X^6 \to \mathbb{R}, which represents energy or potential in the Void. * Morse Indices: Calculate the Morse indices (\operatorname{index}(p)) at each critical point p. '''The Imaginary Medium''' is one of three «worlds», other two being the «written» world and [[The Monoverse]]. One could say that this world is metaphorically lies between them, but this is an inaccuracy. '''The Imaginary Medium''' isn’t «located» between certain the two other worlds, but rather it’s properties can be considered a hybrid between two.

== Description ==
'''The Imaginary Medium''' refers to location of thoughts and in itself can be considered a thought. While «written» world and [[The Monoverse]] contains objects that have a different state of «being written», if this category is even applicable, this «verse» contains every thought in it’s true state. Thoughts are not objects in the usual sense of the word, since they don’t exist. The objects commonly referred to as «thoughts» are a certain sequence of electrical impulses, that are not a thought. We interpretate these sequence as «thoughts» since our brain was designed to, not because sequences itself represent or mean something. This process stays the same, no matter how advanced or primordial the way to think becomes, because they will still only imitate the thoughts themselves. Every attempt to materialize thoughts in the end only results in materializing of the objects meant by them, not them becoming a real object.

'''The Imaginary Medium''' is a boundless place where thoughts form. From the perspective of other worlds, '''The Imaginary Medium''' don’t exist, since it is can be also represented is one, boundless and shapeless thought, from which new form. Every object from [[The Monoverse]] and the «written» world is present here in the form, imagined by the subject who caused that thought to appear. These objects are not the same as in the «written» world and is in [[The Monoverse]], as the act of thinking makes the object less defined than its original copy. Objects can have different properties, varying strictly from the perspective, knowledge and individual thought. However, they will be not the same as their original counterpart, as achieving infinite accuracy in representing certain object (even when trying to replicate not-accurate representation of object) by thinking about it is analogous to writing an infinitely accurate description of it.

There is no boundary to '''The Imaginary Medium''' not because of its size which can’t be limited, but because it doesn’t exist. There are many manifestations of such non-existent object in Hypercosmos, but all of them exist. Even the absolute nothingness, which in itself is considered to be the absolute limit of other worlds exists. Nothingness in two worlds is considered absolute, because it allows everything to exist. These objects, however, are still real in their worlds and are not fictional, while '''The Imaginary Medium''' is. It is imaginary and not real, which puts it into an isolated state where only it can be and nothing else. Such state is analogous to a number in a numerical system without a number of numbers. '''Medium''' will be always considered fictional from the perspective of every object, even if it is located inside it. This is true, because of the fact that '''Medium''' represents the thoughts, which are fictional, but also contains them, which needs it to be fictional. Only an object that is a part of '''Medium''' can be located inside it, but the only object which can do this is thoughts, which are also '''The Imaginary Medium''' itself. The term «fiction» refers to thoughts themselves, not to usual «written» fiction. 

Yet, '''The Imaginary Medium''' is not representation of nothingness, ineffability, transcendence or other such concepts. It can be compared to the endlessly boiling soup without a structure and without anything that composes it. Endlessly many thoughts and fictional versions of real objects, disappearing the same time they’ve appeared. Inside the Medium, every object can have a boundless number of different meanings, properties and abilities. Weakest entity could become the strongest, and the strongest one the weakest. Object can become an entirely different thing in a different thought and then become itself again. This, however, does not allow objects to become «written» or enter [[The Monoverse]], since '''The Imaginary Medium''' is fully disconnected from both of them. Closest we have to '''The Imaginary Medium''' is our imagination, which allows us to think, contain and change the same way the '''Medium''' does it. Dreams can also be used to see something similar to the '''Medium''' structure, but thoughts do it better.

== Epigraph ==
'''The Monorealm''', also known as The Monoverse and the un«written» world is a conceptual object that bears some of the traits of verses. It can’t be considered a part of hierarchies, other verses or chains, due to the properties described down below. Furthermore, it doesn’t contain any normal objects or information about them, instead containing only the undescribed (explained below) parts of them. Though untrue, simply put, '''The Monorealm''' encompasses all undescribed definitions/states of any put object. This process is described in detail in the next chapter of the article and in the section about the '''Voidance''', as it is impossible to define it using simple terms like that before.

=== Explanation ===
Every fictional object has its description or definition; therefore, it exists. It is impossible to write the object or without them, because the reader will simply not know about their existence. Technically, even a name or a blank character in a description counts as a description, even it holds no information about the subject, because it still applies to something. That principle is the reason why it is impossible to write or describe a truly indescribable object. This paradox has been explained multiple times earlier, but it isn’t a reason nor explanation for what '''The Monorealm''' is.

Our understanding of objects stops at the same time its description stops. Every description of fictional or real object is bound to be untrue, because for it to be true, it will need to include the information of everything referred to or affected by that object. In the case of fictional characters, our scope of knowledge about them is even more limited, as pool of information is even smaller than in case of real objects. Everything aside that is covered by our imagination. Or is it?

Even though we will never know a real state of objects and it almost certainly can’t exist, we know that object themselves exists. We know that objects we don’t know about exist, and they can exist, as there nothing stopping them from. After the reader finished reading a book or article, they cannot gain any new information from it. But the fictional world of that book doesn’t disappear or stop updating after every event of the book, even though we can’t view and can’t know everything about it anymore. But it still there, existing in some form.

== Description ==
'''The Monorealm''' is a «verse» that contains every such «real» object there is. While our understanding about cosmic objects is currently limited at {{NUMBEROFARTICLES}} articles describing them, '''The Monorealm''' contains boundless number of them and it is boundless in itself. It cannot be contained by normal verses or ruled by usual entities, as they exist in a separate part of world that has been «written». Such «written» objects have the exact, but infinitely detailed copy somewhere in '''The Monorealm''', existing outside of its original counterpart. Because of that, describing the parts of '''The Monorealm''' or its inhabitants removes the described part or inhabitant, moving them back to the «written» world. However, it does not make '''The Monorealm''' any smaller, since the moved object still has unwritten parts, that make an exact «true» copy inside '''Monorealm'''. Interestingly enough, describing any parts of '''The Monorealm''' makes it grow with the «written» world. '''Monorealm''' also contains «imagined» copies of objects from the «written» world, existing as our only way to speculate about the undescribed and undefined «true» versions.

[[File:The Monoverse.jpg|thumb|263x263px|The artistic illustration of The Monoverse.]]

Once an object is described in normal world by being «written», it transitions from '''The Monorealm''' to the «written» world, while also leaving a boundless array of the «true» copies. Because of that and aforementioned properties, '''The Monorealm''' can be contained only by itself, as every other object is contained inside it in form of its «true» state. These «true» objects aren’t indescribable or ineffable in some way and they don’t have any manifestations, because that would imply that they had a definition. Because they are un«written» and never had definition in first place, we can only know about their existence by names that we assign to them. The name can be assigned to the «true» state of object only in two cases – it is a «true» state of named object, or we want to name it by the concept it refers to. Still, we can refer only to «written» objects, because giving them name makes them «written».

We can’t access '''The Monoverse''' and its inhabitants can’t access our «written» world. They live in the exact way we live, but we can’t know anything about how they do. Still, '''The Monoverse''' is not a full copy of our world, because it has more possibilities than our «written» world has. The closest thing we have to '''The Monoverse''' is our ability to think, because it to some extent replicates Monoverse properties: our mind can imagine the un«written» things, that don’t exist in the normal world, and according to the know data we may theorize about the things we don’t know and can, or don’t exist. '''The Monoverse''' contains exact same entities we know about, yet also contains entities we haven’t found yet and never will. By using '''The Monoverse''' we may learn the existence of the most powerful entity, and the weakest one, we may found largest verse and the smallest one, but we will never truly know anything about them until we will make them «written» and describe them. And by doing so, we already place them in boundaries and make them weaker than those inside '''The Monoverse''', those, about who we will never know.

Technically, this description and the entire page is dedicated to describing «false» '''Monoverse''', since the «real» '''Monoverse''' page will be never written due to '''The Monoverse''' properties. The understanding of '''The Monoverse''' by the regular entities will be never described too, even if one does so (example – the dialogue in the beginning of this page). To them, '''The Monoverse''' and the regular world will be identical, and they will never know any difference. The only way for them to know about '''The Monoverse''' is to use it as thought experiment for acknowledging the existence of un«written» entities.

Following section of article contains information about '''The Monoverse''' properties and history.

== Properties and history ==

=== Properties ===

==== Recursiveness ====
'''The Monoverse''' structure is recursive and self-additive, starting to be like that from the moment this article firstly appeared. From the time first «written» copy of '''The Monoverse''' appeared, it started to boundlessly recurse into itself. These copies weren’t contained inside the main «verse», instead instantly merging into it and becoming one with it. They are still considered separate structures within '''The Monoverse''', even though the one difference between them is the existence of such structures and non-existence.

==== Voidance ====
The main property of '''The Monoverse''' explained in the article is the '''Voidance''', and can be defined as «every object that exists in '''The Monoverse''' has been not «written»». This label can be explained this way – imagine a book with any genre. The book describes a fictional world with fictional characters and fictional objects. The reader’s only way to know about that fictional world and it’s containing is to read the information and text given in the book. That information and text is called the «Written» world. Yet, the information about this world given in the book can’t be fully true, since it describes only a infinitely small part of that fictional book. Even a full description of one fictional character would require to include an infinite amount of information about it, since the writer will need to describe every particle, thought, experience, the full life and death of this character and so on. This un«written» «true» version of the fictional character will be located in the «true» version of fictional world, that is located somewhere in '''The Monoverse'''. The Monoverse itself is always voidant and contains all voidant objects.

===== Strong Voidance =====
'''Voidance''' can be divided into two separate categories – strong and weak voidance. '''Strong Voidance''' is a category applicable to all objects in '''The Monoverse''' that don’t have an index and don’t have a «written» counterpart. '''Index''' is an indicator that allows us to refer to these objects. There are many types of indexes, such as names, descriptions, text and so on. Every index always refers to a copy of certain object in the «written» world and never refers to an object inside The '''Monoverse'''. Almost all objects in '''The Monoverse''' are known by their indexes, until they become «written». Same indexes can refer to multiple objects that have the quality defined in the index, but they can never mean the same objects. Such, the index «Ring» can mean the boundless number of ring-shaped objects, ring verses and etc., but almost certainly never refers to two separate objects inside this category. Objects with '''Strong Voidance''' can’t be bounded by any sort of description, thus becoming truly boundless in the sense of possibilities, properties and abilities they can have. Objects with properties allowed by the strong voidance but not allowed by the «written» world, are considered unique to '''The Monoverse'''.

Strongly-voided objects are not ineffable: ineffability as a category almost certainly don’t exists in '''The Monoverse''', since it contains all «true» states of the objects. This can be illustrated by taking an ineffable object from the «written» world (example [[( )]] or [[The It-That-Is]]), and then comparing to its counterpart from The Imaginary Medium and '''The Monoverse'''. As [[The It-That-Is]] or [[( )]] can be compared to a neverending ladder of avatars, where next avatar describes the previous one, existing at the edge of possibilities given by the «written» world and possibly beyond, it's imaginary counterparts are incomplete and depend on the observer understanding of the object, '''The Monoverse''' counterparts depict their un«written» nature, as they exist beyond the scope the reader and its imagination can see. Every ineffable object would have its strongly-voided or weakly-voided copy in '''The Monoverse''' that can be described. '''The Monoverse''' also allows the existence of truly ineffable (from the view of the «written» world) objects, without any indexes, labels or counterpart in the «written» world. These objects, though, don’t have any effect in The Monoverse, since the ineffability label itself doesn’t make an object an object, without the object meaning itself something more than ineffable.

===== Weak Voidance =====
Weakly-voided objects are voided objects that can have an index or not, but always have a copy in the «written» world. Currently there are {{NUMBEROFARTICLES}} such objects in '''The Monoverse''', if only considering the number of known cosmic objects and nothing else. They can be simply described as infinitely precise, «true» versions of the objects in the «written» world. This page describes a weakly-voided copy of '''The Monoverse''' that exists as a copy of true weakly-voided copy of '''The Monoverse''' in the «written» world and so on. There is not much more information that can be said about weakly-voided objects, aside from the fact that every weakly-voided object also can be considered partially ineffable by default – entities can still have some sort of knowledge about them by using indexes, the «written» information and object copies from The Imaginary Medium.

=== History ===
'''The Monoverse''' always existed in some form. However, that existence was accessible only to the inhabitants of the '''Monoverse''' and no one more. To the current entities, however, nothing was real. Because nothing was «written», the «written» world existed only as a strongly-voided copy inside '''The Monoverse'''. And '''The Monoverse''' itself existed as a strongly-voided copy inside itself, that also contained itself in a recursive structure. Verse started splitting the same time the «written» world and [[The Imaginary Medium]] appeared. It is unknown how this did happen, since none of the beings inside '''The Monoverse''' was able to access any worlds above it. Yet, it did happen. Possibly, one of the objects inside The Monoverse was finally «written» somewhere and did go to the new world. Nonetheless, a new state of existence formed and after some time it started to fill.

For the first time, the «written» world and '''The Monoverse''' were almost identical to each other. However, the first didn’t contained anything except from itself, where The Monoverse contained objects which in future will be integrated to the «written» world. After some time, the «written» state started to expand, «writing» into itself new and new objects from the main world. After some time, it has successfully implemented the ability to exist, which allowed to form many «ineffable» base objects as [[True Nothing (true)]], [[The It-That-Is]], [[( )]]… And after that, the state became self-fulfilling, emerging to what we know as existence.

''To us, however, the history of '''The Monoverse''' starts from the time this document is finished. Before that, the verse «written» copy did never appear in this world. Our goal was to test the limits of our consciousness, and we possibly did it. Maybe, as our mind evolves, we may comprehend concepts vaster than the unknown part of «written» world '''The Monoverse''' is. But, as for now, that remains a mystery. However, we now know who we really are – beings split into three separate worlds, but only able to comprehend fully one of them. Did this discovery was needed? Maybe, if I didn’t write this exact document and didn’t took part in the «Monoverse» project, I was able to evade this fate? Still, I think that this question does not matter, as I can now see the true nature of the world, I’m currently in – frozen, unchanging and slow. And that will stay this way until everything goes to black again. Until I stop existing.''

Perhaps one of the most important reality stabilizers in almost all [[Physical Realm|First Realms]], the '''''Trees''''' are cosmic bodies that not only have an existence-smoothing effect inside their plethora of branches, but outside of them as well, with the chain of containment letting the Trees' energy permeate throughout their local First Realm. 

The Trees have [[Verse|verses]] within them that are the same as those of the Branches, in greater quantity of course, and other Trees around them are all connected by roots, however the links are very thin and Trees are separated based on the thinnest part of their roots.  

== Stability of Trees and Branches ==
The stabilization of physics, math, and other extremely fundamental forces or objects such as [[Primordium Particles]] stem from the roots of the Trees and go up the trunk into their [[The Branch|Branches]], hence why lower ones are far more stable. 

Speaking of stability, despite the Trees' effects on everything, the fact they at this point are the containees greatly weaken their power across the First realms, although still noticable compared to the frighteningly odd [[The Second Realm|Second Realms]]. Of course, all beyond those are much more unstable and bizarre, but not as much as they could be. 

== Nicknames ==
Due to their importance, the Trees have gained nicknames such as "The Plants of our Ways," "The 0.5th [[Everything Layer|Everything Layers]]", and other very positive titles. 

== Trivia ==

* No extremely large-sized [[:Category:Cosmic entity|organisms]] lay here, as the Trees don't bear [[:Category:Cosmic Food|fruits]] or have any nutritional value, as their insides fully consist of inedible [[The Sap|sap]].

== About == '''The Upper Bound''' is the '''definitive supremum''' of [[All dimensions Wiki]]. Operating within the transcendent boundaries of '''Class ω''', it represents the first true limit ordinal of the hierarchy spectrum. It is not an archverse or a spatial container, but the absolute mathematical ceiling that encapsulates the entirety of all conceptual, logical, and structural realities. While standard meta-structures are bound to finite numerical tiers, The Upper Bound treats the entire infinite sequence of preceding classes as an infinitesimal, zero-dimensional point. Everything in existence—including [[The Box]], the infinite clusters of [[Omniverse]]s, [[The Drum]], all numerical hierarchies, and all higher-class systems—is nested inside its absolute horizon. == The Asymptotic Expansion Paradox: The Scene of All Existence == === It is everything === The Upper Bound is absolutely everything that exists; '''it is not matter, instead it is where matter acts'''. Within the rigid architecture of Class ω, it does not function as a standard physical entity or a cosmic substance. Instead, it serves as the ultimate spatial and logical framework—the primordial scene where all dimensional, metaphysical, and conceptual interactions are forced to take place. Because it is the absolute foundation of logic itself, '''no structural tier can exist separate from its parameters'''. It is '''the boundless stage''' that allows the entire hierarchy spectrum, from the smallest multi-universal units to the absolute infinity of the Omniverses, to have a structural reality. === The Adaptive Horizon Paradox === When something new is invented which is supposedly "''past The Upper Bound''", The Upper Bound '''instantly expands and goes to contain that'''; it is the scene. This property establishes a supreme cosmological rule known as the ''Adaptive Supremum Horizon''. Because it operates as the true transfinite completion, it cannot be outscaled by the creation of higher mathematical classes, cardinallities, or custom fanon verses. The moment an external structure is conceived by any entity or editor attempting to transcend the known boundaries, a non-reciprocal conceptual absorption occurs. The Upper Bound does not fight or resist this expansion; instead, '''its absolute mathematical perimeter scales automatically and infinitely to encompass the new data'''. Consequently, the newly invented reality is instantly stripped of its transcendent status and is pre-deterministically reclassified as a minor internal subset, operating safely within the eternal and inescapable theater of the Limit Class. == Mechanics of the Transfinite Ceiling == The Upper Bound operates via three fundamental cosmic laws that prevent any form of external expansion: === Asymptotic Supremum === Unlike regular structures where containment implies physical volume, The Upper Bound contains reality through conceptual exhaustion. Every verse or archverse that expands "infinitely" is actually just moving asymptotically closer to this boundary. No matter how large a structure grows—even if it utilizes hyper-exponential layers or transfinites beyond any notation—'''it remains mathematically bounded''' and dwarfed by the absolute threshold of Class ω. === Dimensional Collapse === Inside the core of The Upper Bound, the concept of [[Dimension]]ality ceases to exist. While advanced structures require complex axes to remain stable, Class ω transcends active coordinates entirely. It is a state of '''absolute geometric singularity where all mathematical dimensions are compressed''' into a single, indivisible logical node, making it '''completely impenetrable for lower-order entities''' or cosmic overseers. === The Non-Reciprocal Filter === The Upper Bound functions as a one-way mathematical wall. Energy, information, and collapsing realities can expand outward toward the horizon, but nothing can ever breach or cross outside its boundary, because there is '''no "outside"''' to transition into. It is the absolute framework that seals all potential realities, preventing the entirety of the cosmic spectrum from dissolving into true mathematical nothingness. == See Also == * [[The Box]] * [[Omniverse]] * [[The Drum]] * [[Class Categories]] * [[The Official Hierarchy]]

The '''''Timelineverse''''' acts like a time-dimensional type of [[universe]] with 2D time instead of 1D time. The Timelineverse is a part of every single universe, as each universe allows for different timelines and versions of itself, and is linked to the [[The Time Tree|Time Tree]]. The Timelineverse does not take up space as it is purely time. The horizontal axis of the Timelineverse (each 1D piece of time on the plane) can be referred to as the T axis, and the vertical axis of the Timelineverse (the 1D shift between timelines) can be referred to as the L axis.

With the extra dimension of time, there can be infinite variations of any universe, as timelines create and branch due to any actions that could occur. For example, life forms in this universe on a different timeline can already have technology impossible in our timeline as anything can happen in any timeline in this universe, an infinite amount of timelines have extremely advanced technology, an infinite amount don't, etc. Another infinite amount probably don't even have life in the first place. Essentially, the Timelineverse follows the traditional idea of the multiverse (the [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Many-worlds_interpretation Many-Worlds Interpretation], where every action leads to a split/branching universe) however shows it purely thru timelines. However, some timelines are purely made because our universe formation/singularity had been different in that timeline in comparison to other timelines. 

Without any sort of “timeline traveling” device which can traverse the L axis, we normally are not able to see any of the timelines, but if we did have this kind of a device then we would see that all of the timelines are like branches, assembled in a Yggdrasil tree.

Every single Timelineverse has links to the [[Cloudverse]], as the many Timelineverse has a sort of time wormhole that souls pass through when a person passes away, as to allow for ease of use, each Timelineverse immediately teleports a soul to the Cloudverse.

== About size ==
If you move at least a little along the second time coordinate, then you will leave your timeline and either get into another one (depending on the distance between the timelines) or into a void where there seems to be time, but there is only emptiness. So in fact, to calculate the size of this universe, we need to square the size of the ordinary universe, then we will cover the size of all timelines + "time voids".

== UNI-5039 ==
UNI-5039 is known to be the closest [[universe]] to our own, at 1.1 trillion light-years from it. It is part of the [[Local Universe Group]]. UNI-5039 is home to over 2000 known civilizations, with the most advanced one being a 3.4 on the Kardashev scale. It is about 43 billion years old. It has almost 8 trillion galaxies, 1 sextillion stars, and 936 octillion planets. Its name comes from it being the 5,039th Universe documented by [[Human|humans]], but was the first explored by humans. The reason it was discovered so late was due to the positioning of UNI-5039 and the telescopes used to detect Universes. UNI-5039 was almost impossible to see on the planets where the telescopes were put, but eventually it was found after they decided to put one on one of the other planets.

=== Formation ===
This Universe was formed 43 billion years ago. It had its own big bang, due to the high concentration of matter in the [[Inertio Supernebula]] (which also created [[our Universe]] and [[UNI-3]]), and  it expanded a lot. After cooling down and expanding more, it became the universe that is there today. It will die out in a 100 trillion years, when all matter in this universe will die.

=== Civilizations ===
There are over 2000 known civilizations in this Universe, so I won’t name all of them.

The most common civilizations are a type 0.2, with only one civilization being a 3.4. The 3.4 civilization is known as the [[Tuhis]](Too-is) and are so advanced I literally cannot explain it other than they rule over multiple [[Galaxy|galaxies]]. Fortunately, they know not to interact with humans as humans almost wiped out half their species in a war.

===Contents===

*It is smaller than the Unifield.

A Vendekaverse is a cluster of [[Quettaverse|Quettaverses]]. Spacetime is distorted enough that gravity pulls things "randomly" depending on their position. <u>'''! WARNING !''' Building large structures inside the Vendekaverse is extremely dangerous! The extreme gravitational forces may rip apart your structure. Additionally, sufficiently large disturbances may destroy the Vendekaverse.</u>

==='''Form of the Vendekaverse'''===
To prevent the Vendekaverse from exploding into a giant mess, [[Gravityverse|Gravityverses]] absorb the extreme gravity forces and redirect them to stay mostly normal. These Extraverses appear in those ‘blobs’ you see in the image. However, these are actually portals into the [[Nowhereverse]], so be careful! There can be any number of ‘blobs’, sizes of them, etc, but generally the larger and outer ones tend to be more stable. The other matter tends to be [[Universe|Universes]] and the luminosity is mostly larger bodies exploding as they enter the Vendekaverse’s extreme gravitational field, due to the [[Extraverse]]s spewing them out. The extremely large of the Vendekaverses (300 Sexdecillion & larger) have even been seen to have over 4,752 blobs, most of them being incredibly tiny though. 

Civilizations colonizing the Vendekaverse have created technologies to jump not only Quettaverses but also blobs, and civilizations controlling it may even be able to rearrange the entire verse using the [[Gravityverse|Gravityverses]].

The '''''Versiumverse''''' or '''''Uniumverse''''' is a sort of a cosmic building block of the [[Omniumverse]]. Versiumverses in a [[Multiumverse]] share commons laws of physics, and systems of logic, but differ in initial starting conditions upon being formed, and thus have entirely different timelines.

Versiumverses, unlike all Archiumverses after them, aren't made out of other verses, but instead, cosmic structures, elementary particles, and just generally all are [[Verse|absolutely verse]]. Uniumverses differ very slightly in size and average out in the 100 billion light-year range.

Each Uniumverse has a set of laws that govern everything inside without exception. Their laws can be broken, however, objects aren't actively breaking a law at any time. They simply [[Existence Rank|stop existing]] or stop being [[Containment|contained]] by the Uniumverse, as to counteract the law-breaking.

The laws in a Universe also typically only govern [[Blueprint Particle|properties]] of objects within the said Universe, instead of primarily governing [[laws]] of inferior objects, but Uniumverses can change laws of inferior objects.

==Uniumverse Border==
The border of a Uniumverse is located at the boundary of its sphere of law influence. Uniumverses may not have physical borders, as in our Uniumverse, whose boundary is pushed by dark energy continuously further away and the border is simply a cut-off for our law systems.

Universe borders, at least the ones similar to ours, have some sort of a negative of matter, energy, and spacetime. It is also possible that all structures will be destroyed instantaneously, without any forewarning. are expanded by a force that either acts solely on the border, or one that occurs naturally but also interacts with the border as well, but Uniumverses Retract the same way.

Borderless Uniumverses, those in the form of [[Verse|UILNB-2n]], usually lose their border rather than having it be absent from the Uniumverses very conception. This does not mean that the Uniumverse’s laws influence indefinitely far, as in, being borderless, but that they don't end abruptly but fizzle out. These types of Uniumverses don't exactly have any special phenomena happing at the "fuzzy area" that could implicate a border either, but one can see from a far that the Uniumverse’s structures simply fizzle out after a certain distance from the center.

Uniumverses and Universes are not the Same but also not different.

== About ==
The '''''Variedverse''''' is similar to the [[yourmomverse|Yourmomverses]], but instead of only containing variations of mothers, it contains variations of all known [[:Category:Cosmic entity|entities]]. The Variedverse has too many states to list, but the most notable ones will be summarized below;
#The Variedverse likely existed long before even several [[The First Boom|First Booms]], so it's basically impossible to tell what it's first state was.  However, the first ever recorded state of the Variedverse was in a Mucube-like formation.  Not much is known about this state, other than it was the state of the Variedverse approximately 0.007 [[Voidsecond|voidseconds]] after the First Boom that led to our local [[Cetaverse]]'s creation, and that only a few entities likely existed in it.
#142 [[OYC]] after the state of the variedverse completely shifted around constantly, there was an entire week where it maintained one position; the triangle. It's unconfirmed why it kept this shape for so much longer than others, but it's theorized that it was likely due to the triangle having the strongest molecular structure out of any shape, which allowed it to maintain it's position for awhile.
#Another notable state occured 2,022 OYC later than the previous notable state; where it maintained a state for 12.32 seconds. This is the 2nd longest that the variedverse has maintained one solid shape.  It's also noteworthy due to this being the first time it shifted into a 4 dimensional shape;  A petrial tesseract, to be exact.
#The most notable state is likely when it suddenly became Ω-Dimensional, turning into an Apeirosphere. This lasted for 172 voidseconds, as opposed to the regular 1 voidsecond.  This is the 18th longest that a singular state has existed. This likely occurred when all entities fused into one, trying to escape, so it transformed temporarily to something that they couldn't escape.

==Interesting Variations of Entities==
There have been more and more variations of several entities throughout the past couple million OYC.  Here's some of the most common and interesting ones. 

==Alphasms==
While the normal [[Alphasm|Alphasms]] usually are not directly contained within this [[verse]], all other variations and avatars of them are contained here. This includes, but is not limited to;

*Deleted Alphasms.
*Old Versions of Alphasms.
*Future Versions of Alphasms.

Wikiverse}}The '''''Wikiverse''''' is basically the entire wiki, containing every page, template, and category that we can view on the wiki. They also sometimes contain [[Transcendent Omni-God]]s, though them traveling between Wikiverses is possible and common. The Wikiverses can also have their smaller versions, known as the [[Fake Wikiverse|Fake Wikiverses]].

There could be something larger, <s><small>like the [[FANDOMverse]]</small></s> we just do not know yet.
==[[Pageverse|Pageverses]]==

A Pageverse is a bubble-like [[:Category:Structure|structure]] which usually has a red glow on it. They also have several sections that have a varying amount of verses within them which can be so big it ends up being undefined. Pageverses are usually connected to [[Categoryverse|Categoryverses]] or different Pageverses with meta strings, however these connections are very loose and hard to follow. Otherwise, they just float around in their Wikiverses.

If a Pageverse describes something badly or doesn't give enough information on something, the object may be fuzzy in the cosmology until it is made clearer by other [[TOG|TOGs]].

=== Home Pageverse ===
A home Pageverse is the largest Pageverse in terms of size in its Wikiverse. It has randomized and/or popular page links, a link to the discussions, and several other things as well.

==Categoryverses ==

Categoryverses/Categories are glowing green Pageverses that sometimes have letters inside them, though most don't. They are also another key part of webs, and connect many Pageverses together.

==Templates==

Templates are glowing blue pageverses that can replace certain arrangements of letters in other pages into portions of the template's letters with certain inputs. These arrangements that are connected to templates (if made by a Transcendent Omni-God) always start with "<nowiki>{{</nowiki>" and end with "<nowiki>}}</nowiki>". They usually aren’t connected directly to categories, however, most are connected to webs through pageverses that use them.

==The Editor==

The editor is a verse that Transcendent Omni-Gods teleport to in order to change the text in a Pageverse, template, category, or more. Some transcendent omni-gods are restricted from certain sections of the editor. It glows pink in the Wikiverse and you might find many Transcendent Omni-Gods inside The Editor.

==Transcendent Omni-Gods==

''For more info on Transcendent Omni-Gods, see [[Transcendent Omni-God|this page]].''

Transcendent Omni-Gods are basically sentient auras that control the Wikiverse and have different levels of power and superiority. They also sometimes contain a yellow page called a Transcendent Omni-Note.

===Transcendent Omni-Notes===

Transcendent omni-notes are yellow-colored areas containing an image of a Transcendent Omni-God, some info on them, and some large signs above the profile telling you about their statuses or rights. There are several portals to rooms within Transcendent Omni-Notes, known as profiles, which are just simply profiles that tell you a lot more about them, message walls, which are walls that you can write on that they will check every so often and see them, blog posts, which contain blogs that contain various stuff that the ToGs want to say, and contributions, which explains the ToG’s history. Most of these sections are purple and sometimes link to other things, such as categories, permanently connecting the ToG to the Wikiverse and combining with their soul. These ToGs are known as “users”.

==Discussions==
The discussions is a gray verse where ToGs chat with each other. It is often used for random polls as well. It mostly just floats around in the Wikiverse. It isn’t hard to find though, as it is linked through by the huge, red main page.

== The Trashcan ==

The trashcan is a verse that contains every deleted page and thus every object in the cosmology deleted by TOGs. Some pages may be spam and don't define any form of object, or other pages in the trashcan actually define something, and these things weren't deemed clear enough to be in the cosmology. It is a glowing white trapezoid. If another pageverse outside the trashcan tries to link to another pageverse inside the trashcan or that never existed at all, it will result in a red link, that cannot be followed. Red links redirect you to The Editor where you can bring back the pageverse starting from scratch. This is different from the [[Removed Universe]], as this contains every deleted page in the wiki while the Removed Universe contains everything defined from deleted pages in this wiki.

There is also an autofill system for thing in the trashcan affecting other things. If A is superior to B on some scale, and C is inferior to B on the same scale, but B is in the trashcan, it will autofill the gap between A and C using a placeholder going by the same name as B. This placeholder is a completely plain void or a standard entity with no personality, and cannot be changed by TOGs unless a TOG brings back B from the trashcan.

== Growth ==
The wikiverse, as well as everything outside it, keeps getting bigger. The size is increased by [[The Absolute - ƒ|ƒ]] times it’s previous size ƒ times per planck time. Once, in 647 OYC, it stopped growing until 2 ToGs, named “Randomuser66” and “Oofandfoo” fixed it.

== Dead Wikiverse ==
Many wikiverses are dead, having zero growth and no active TOGs. Dead wikiverses are extremely still and are ultimately limited. [[:Category:Object|Objects]], [[:Category:Cosmic entity|entities]], and [[Verse|verses]] upon appearing in a dead wikiverse are deprived of TOGs, and have their entire existence be limited. Some entities jump to dead wikiverses just to escape TOG control.

== Hyper-chungusverse ==
The Hyper-chungusverse experiment is an exploitation of poor wording that allows for the containment of the Wikiverse inside of an All Dimensions wiki cosmological object. The achievement of this involves the process of imagining an object called “entire wiki” with its properties as “Is equal to Wikiverse, and the only object called entire wiki, also can be referred to as wiki”. We then proceed by imagining a “Hyper-chungusverse” with its only property as “contains entire wiki”. We then imagine that an entity within All Dimensions thinks of this, and that the “Hyper-chungusverse” is the verse that is here, on the Wikiverse page.

This works because of a combination of properties in the All Dimensions wiki. In this wiki, we have objects such as [[The Box|Boxes]] which contain real and imaginary objects. This implies that objects that are imagined still exist within the All Dimensions wiki. Secondly, on the Wikiverse page, it says that it is basically the entire wiki, without saying which wiki it is. This allows for the assumption that it contains an “entire wiki”, which, because of the “the” must be the only one. Finally, the “Hyper-chungusverse” is not described in any detail here, only the “Hyper-chungusverse experiment”. This basically allows the Hyper-chungusverse as a blank slate that we can imagine properties onto. (this is similar to the “entire wiki”, it says it is basically the entire wiki, without saying anything about what the entire wiki is. Stating the entire wiki with the properties previously stated is not paradoxical because it has all the properties the Wikiverse says it does.)

However, writing about it on All Dimensions wiki places it in a pageverse of the Wikiverse, so this verse cannot be written about to not be contained by the Wikiverse. Unfortunately, it is written about here, and thus it is contained by a pageverse, and thus contained by the Wikiverse.

== About ==
A '''''wormhole''''' is a topological hole in the manifold of [[Universe|spacetime]]. Advanced [[:Category:Civilization|civlizations]] commonly use them in order to travel to different locations in space time, but it can be extremely risky to use too much of them as it might corrupt the universe they are being used in. Its size and shape depends on its universes qualities. It can only be used on universes, but certain technology is being made to expand that.

Wormholes can vary from a measly [[string]] linkage across spacetime to a large 100,000 light years, but they usually all look the same when they are used. An endless quantity of wormholes can be extracted from the quantum foam through extremely advanced [[:Category:Technology|technology]].

== History of Wormholes ==

* Back when our [[Omniverse]] was first created, lots of [[Archverse|archverses]] started to appear inside them. Wormholes first started to appear in [[Hyperverse|hyperverses]], then eventually everywhere in the omniverse. Life in this Omniverse started harvesting them for teleportation, [[:Category:War|war]], and more, and they soon realized that they were destroying dimensions around them.
* Several wars started to break out between dimensions and [[Interdimensional Void|Interdimensional Voids]]. This started a huge war that thousands of [[Universe|universes]] participated in, called the ''Great Wormhole War''. It ended in wormholes being prohibited to most [[:Category:Cosmic entity|entities]], and after that, only entities far up in the [[The Official Hierarchy|hierarchy]] were allowed to use wormholes.
* After that, wormholes started to be rediscovered by the more common lifeforms, so very powerful entities prohibited their use for a while. However, one powerful entity went rogue and started destroying tons of universes with wormholes. This sparked another wormhole war, but thankfully, it luckily didn’t last very long this time.

== Omniversal Wormholes ==
Wormholes are currently being developed that are meant to carry entities to any archverse possible. For example: a hyperverse to a [[metaverse]], or a [[multiverse]] to a universe. Not many tests have been done with them, though, since they're in an extremely early development stage.
